The Bouda Artillery Fortress is one of the most intact facilities remaining - despite the notable evidence of shelling.

properties.name: Hanička (dělostřelecká tvrz)
properties.street: Rokytnice v Orlických horách 70, 517 61 Rokytnice v Orlických horách, Czechia
properties.description: The Hanička artillery fortress of the 1930s Czecoslovak fortifications was converted into a nuclear fallout shelter. The underground tour will take you between three separate interlinked artillery fortresses in the forest - but there are many more bunkers just off the main road.

properties.name: Chráněná krajinná oblast Broumovsko
properties.description: Sandstone spires form a city of pinnacles in the Broumovsko Protected Landscape Area, including the Adršpach-Teplice Rocks, Broumovské stěny, and Teplické skály.

properties.name: Stachelberg (dělostřelecká tvrz)
properties.description: The interconnected bunkers of the Stachelburg Artillery Fort was part of the Czechoslovakia Border Fortifications intended to defend against Nazi invasion -  only for it to be handed over to the Nazis without a fight following the Munich Betrayal. This is the largest fortress in Czechia, and features hiking trails between even more bunkers.

properties.name: Čertovy hlavy
properties.description: It's Mt. Rushmore, except haunted and Czech. In the 1840s a Czech artist carved terrifying massive faces into the stone. The weathering has made the carvings appear even more discomforting.

properties.name: Chráněná krajinná oblast Český ráj
properties.description: Czech Paradise Protected Landscape Area is teeming with sandstone pinnacles and historical castles. This includes the Prachov Rocks, Příhrazské rocks, Hruboskalsko, and the Trosky castle ruins located on top of an extinct volcano.

properties.name: Chráněná krajinná oblast Labské pískovce
properties.description: That's right it's even more beautiful Czech mountains located in the Protected landscape area of Labská pískovec. This is the companion park to the much more popular Bohemian Switzerland National Park. The protected area notably includes the sandstone pillars of Tiské stěny, and the canyons of Kaňon Labe.

properties.name: Muzeum starých strojů a technologií
properties.description: The Museum of Old Machines and Technology is a former Czech textile mill stuffed with 40+ antique cars, 20+ motorcycles, tractors, and locomotives,

properties.name: Národní technické muzeum
properties.description: The Czech National Technical Museum is a sampler of all technologies the Czech have created. In this museum there are cars, trains, and airplanes manufactured in Czechia. Notable exhibits include Austria-Hungarian Emperor Franz Joseph's railcar, and antique vehicles by Tatra and Skoda. For more in depth museums for each of these technologies, consider the Lužná u Rakovníka Railway Museum (trains), Aircraft museum Kbely (planes), and Muzeum starých strojů a technologií (industrial equipment and cars).

properties.name: Armádní muzeum Žižkov
properties.description: Czechia historically was conquered a lot due to being a small nation stuck between the great powers of Europe - so they've done a lot of fighting. The  Žižkov army museum tells the story of the Czech armed forces from the independent Kingdoms of Bohemia and Moravia, to subjugation under the Hapsburg monarchy (and uprising against it during the Bohemian revolt) , to the fight for the Czechoslovak Republic following the collapse of Austria-Hungary, subjugation by the Nazis and Communists (and the revolt of the Prague Spring against communism), and finally modern independence.

properties.name: Národní park České Švýcarsko
properties.description: Czech Switerland National Park is an area full of sandstone arches, gorges, and pillars that line the cliffs of the Elbe mountains.

properties.name: Nationalpark Sächsische Schweiz
properties.description: Saxon Switzerland National Park is composed of rock pillars sticking out of the Elbe mountains. Notably, the Germans built the Bastei bridge through the pillars so you can admire them from the sky.

properties.name: Park vojaške zgodovine Pivka
properties.description: The Pivka Park of Military History is the largest military museum in Slovenia. The museum features a strange mix of United States, Soviet Union, and Yugoslavian military vehicles and airplanes. A unique feature is the Yugoslavian Navy Una-class special operations submarine Zeta on display in the middle of the museum. There's also a 40 minute hike to the WW2 era Italian Alpine Wall Fortifications.

properties.name: Železniški muzej Slovenskih železnic
properties.description: Come see rusty Yugoslavian locomotives and some that are in good condition! The Slovenian Railway Museum features locomotives and equipment from Slovenian History. This includes 60+ locomotives and 50+ vehicles from the Austro-Hungarian Empire, to Yugoslavia, to independence.

properties.name: Regijski park Škocjanske jame
properties.description: The Škocjan Caves Regional Park features a massive underground canyon running through the middle, as well as a near vertical gorge on the exterior. There's also all the stalactites and stalagmites one would expect.

properties.name: Dimnice (jama)
properties.description: Dimnice Cave features a spiral staircase down the vertical mouth of the cave that feels as if you are descending into Hades.

properties.name: Postojnska jama
properties.description: This is THE European cave. The Postojna Cave system is 15 miles of caves full of massive rooms that are so big they feel fake. There are rooms in the cave with space for 10,000+ people that are used as concert halls, towering pillars of stalactites and stalagmites, an underground post office, and electric trains haul tourists through the caverns so they can see all of it.

properties.name: Grad Predjama
properties.description: It's a renaissance castle built into a cave in a cliff.

properties.name: Triglavski narodni park
properties.street: Na logu v Trenti, 5232 Soča, Slovenia
properties.description: Triglav National park is Slovenia's only national park, and is centered around Mount Triglav in the Alps. Notable hikes include the Vintgar gorge, which features a series of wooden walkways to a waterfall.

properties.name: Eigiau Dam
properties.description: The Eigiau Dam failed in 1925, killing 16 people downstream. The dam now sits in ruins near Llyn Eigaiau.

properties.name: Trianon Múzeum
properties.street: Várpalota, Gróf Apponyi Albert liget 1, 8100 Hungary
properties.description: Hungary took the blame at the end of WW1 and was cut down to 1/3 of its pre-war area, with 31% of all Hungarians living outside of the new borders. The treaty has left such lasting resentment that the Trianon museum was opened to showcase the downsides of the treaty.

properties.name: Atomenergetikai Múzeum
properties.description: Come learn about the Hungarian nuclear industry - which is really just a Soviet built reactor. You can see a replica of the the reactor at this museum - but the real thing is just down the road at a secured facility.

properties.name: RepTár Szolnoki Repülőmúzeum
properties.description: This is the Hungarian Aviation Museum. Unfortunately, Hungary doesn't particularly have an aerospace industry, so all the aircraft here are Soviet made.

properties.name: Magyar Vasúttörténeti Park
properties.description: The Hungarian Railway History Park is the main railway museum in Hungary, featuring 100+ railway vehicles from 1870s Austria-Hungary, to Communist domination, to the present. Including the streamlined MAV 242, streamlined Arpad diesel railcar which looks like it inspired the tabletop game Warhammer, and a miniature garden railway which you can ride around on.

properties.name: Hungarian Parliament Building
properties.description: The Hungarian Parliament Building is the defining piece of Gothic Architecture - inside and outside. You will need to reserve a tour in advance.

properties.name: SMS Leitha (1871)
properties.street: Budapest, Id. Antall József rkp., 1055 Hungary
properties.description: The 1871 SMS Leitha was the first river monitor in Europe, it's also the last one afloat.

properties.name: Terror Háza Múzeum
properties.description: During communist rule, Hungary was brutally repressed by the State Protection Authority (ÁVH), attempts at reform were put down by military force during the Hungarian Revolution of 1956. The House of Terror is a memorial to fascist and communist rule and features ÁVH torture cells that tourists can go inside of.

properties.name: Halászbástya
properties.description: The Fisherman's Bastion fortress overlooks the city of Budapest from the west bank of the Danube. The Fortress was rebuilt as a Neo-Romanesque style castle in 1895.

properties.name: Közlekedési Múzeum
properties.description: The Hungarian Technical and Transportation museum shows off Hungarian transportation from carriages to railroads to cars to airplanes. Yes they have the cool streamlined Arpad trains that look straight out of Warhammer.

properties.name: Chráněná krajinná oblast Moravský kras
properties.description: The Moravian Karst Protected Landscape Area covers the gorges and caves of the Moravian Karst - including the famous Macocha Abyss.

properties.name: Dobrošov (dělostřelecká tvrz)
properties.description: Dobrošov Artillery Fortress was part of the Czechoslovak border fortifications designed to protect the country from invasion against Nazi Germany. However, despite promises to defend democratic Czechoslovakia, the United Kingdom and France instead decided to hand over all of the fortifications to the Nazis following the Munich Betrayal. The fortifications of N-D-S 72 Můstek and N-D-S 72 Můstek are kept in great condition, and there are many more bunkers along trails if you want a nice stroll through the Czech countryside. .

properties.name: N-S 82 Březinka
properties.description: N-S 82 Březinka was an infantry blockhouse part of the Czechoslovakian Border Fortifications that were meant to defend the country from Nazi invasion - and they would have if the British and French didn't instead decide to hand the country over to the Nazis. Březinka has been nearly entirely restored - and is in near pristine condition. Because it's part of a continuous line of fortifications, there are trails to even more bunkers and fortresses nearby.

properties.name: Deutsches Marinemuseum
properties.description: The German Naval Museum focuses on the history of the German Navy, and features 5 prominent warships: an East German Libelle class torpedo boat, the Cold War era Type 205 submarine U-10, a Lindau-class minehunter, a Gepard-class fast attack craft, and the Lütjens-class missile destroyer Mölders.

properties.name: Deutsches Schifffahrtsmuseum
properties.description: The German Maritime Museum tells the story of German maritime history - including the bits from 1914-1945. The museum features the WW2 era Type XXI submarine Wilhelm Bauer, the 1924 ocean tug Seefalke, the 1940 whaling ship Rau IX, the 1908 lightship Bürgermeister Abendroth, and some other submarines and hydrofoils inside the museum.

properties.name: Soviet submarine B-515
properties.description: Tour the 1976 Soviet Tango-class submarine B-515, recently renamed U-434. This is the nicest Soviet Submarine in Germany - the other one is much rustier.

properties.name: Historisch-Technisches Museum Peenemünde
properties.description: The Peenemünde Historical Technical Museum is set in an old power station and features the history of the development of modern ballistic rockets. For some reason there's also the Soviet 1963 Juliett-class nuclear ballistic missile submarine U-461 docked nearby, and the Tarantul-class corvette Hans Beilmer.

properties.name: Rostock Schifffahrtsmuseum
properties.description: The Rostock Shipbuilding and Shipping Museum possesses the 1958 East German cargo ship Dresden. See the might of East German shipping.

properties.name: Deutsches Technikmuseum
properties.description: Come see overly complex German technology at the German Museum of Technology. Featuring two railway roundhouses full of 40+ locomotives, 270+ cars, a railcar hall with 50+ municipal transport vehicles, and some planes.

properties.name: Cap San Diego
properties.description: Come see the 1961 museum ship MS Cap San Diego - the pinnacle of West German Shipbuilding before containerization took over the industry.

properties.name: KZ Neuengamme
properties.description: 42,000+ people were killed by the Nazis at Neuengamme Concentration Camp between 1938-and 1945. Those that did survive were put on death marches, or loaded into empty passenger ships that were later sunk. The victorious allies later used the concentration camp as a prison for Nazis, and later as a state prison, then juvenile detention center until 2003.

properties.name: Deutsches Erdölmuseum Wietze
properties.description: The Germans love overly complicated machinery, and overly complicated machinery needs oil to run. Come see how Germany extracted oil at the German Oil Museum. 80% of all German oil production came from the surroundings of this museum. The museum features a lot of really tall oil rigs from 1899-present.

properties.name: Hubschraubermuseum Bückeburg
properties.description: Germany developed the first practical helicopter in 1936, come see the FW 61 and 53+ other helicopters at the Bückeburg Helicopter Museum. The museum also features the first British production helicopter (Bristol 171-Mk. 52), the experimental helicopters of Gerard Georges de Vastey, and the replica of the first helicopter to ever achieve flight in 1907.

properties.name: Externsteine
properties.description: 40-metre sandstone rock pillars carved with religious imagery rise out of the Teutoberg Forest. There's staircases so you can climb to the very top of the spires.

properties.name: LVR-Archäologischer Park Xanten
properties.description: The Roman Empire made it all the way up to Germany, and this archaeological park delves into the remains of the Roman colony of Colonia Ulpia Traiana. The ruins feature a mini version of the Colosseum, a temple, and gatehouse. There's also replicas of Roman ships.

properties.name: Eisenbahnmuseum Bochum
properties.description: The Bochum Railway museum features 120+ rail vehicles from 1853-1976 . Unique exhibits include a maglev, and a railbus - it's literally just a bus with train wheels.

properties.name: Deutsches Bergbau-Museum Bochum
properties.description: The German Mining Museum Bochum is a mine - in the middle of a city. You can learn about German mining, and actually go into the mine itself - which was built explicitly for tourism.

properties.name: Flugausstellung Peter Junior
properties.description: The Peter Junior Air Show is a private air museum with 100+ aircraft, including a replica of the Concorde which has been made into a café. There's also various Soviet and British airliners. The aircraft have very little fencing protecting them, so you can go right up to most of them.

properties.name: Museum für Antike Schifffahrt
properties.description: Come see actual Roman ships! Five Roman ships were discovered near Mainz on the Rhine in 1981, the remains were put inside the Museum of Ancient Seafaring, and full sized replicas were built of each of the ships.

properties.name: Eisenbahnmuseum Darmstadt-Kranichstein
properties.description: The Darmstadt-Kranichstein Railway Museum features 200+ vehicles. It's not the most specialized Railway museum in Germany, but it is one of the biggest.

properties.name: Schloss Bruchsal
properties.description: Sure Castle Bruschal is the really pretty palace of the Prince-Bishopric of the Imperial City of Speyer, but it's also home of the Deutsches Musikautomaten-Museum (German Music Machine Museum) - featuring a replica of the RMS Titanic's organ, and the Municipal History Museum.

properties.name: Dornier Museum Friedrichshafen
properties.description: Dornier was a German aircraft manufacturer from 1914-1996, during their operation Dornier produced massive flying boats, and experimental aircraft. The vertical takeoff cargo aircraft the Do 31, and the flying boats Do24, N25, and some satellites are here at the museum.

properties.name: Schloss Nymphenburg
properties.description: It's Bavarian Versailles. The Nymphenburg Palace was the summer Palace of the King of Bavaria from 1663 until the dissolution of German nobility in 1918. As Bavaria was one of the largest and wealthiest German states, the palace is one of the largest and most opulent. The massive palace complex is filled with museums, including the Museum of Man and Nature, and the Marstallmuseum (carriage museum) featuring 40+ preposterously ornate carriages.

properties.name: KZ Dachau
properties.description: Dachau Concentration Camp was one of the first Nazi concentration camps, and 41,500+ people were killed here either through murder, neglect, or in experiments. After the war the camp was used to hold Nazi war criminals for trial.

properties.name: Kehlsteinhaus
properties.description: The Eagle's Next has a restaurant at the top of a mountain, beautiful trails and a striking view of the mountains and valleys surrounding it. There's a bus from the Dokumentationszentrum that will take you to the elevator if you don't want to do the 4-hour round trip hike.

properties.name: Dokumentationszentrum Reichsparteitagsgelände
properties.description: The Nazi Party Rally Grounds in Nuremburg now lay in ruins like their failed ideology. The Documentation Center on the grounds tells the story of the showmanship and consequences of National Socialism, as well as the Nuremburg Trials where those that committed crimes against humanity met their deserved end.

properties.name: KZ Flossenbürg
properties.description: The Flossenbürg concentration camp killed 30,000 people during the forced labor in the granite quarries and Messerschmitt factories. This is not a happy place.

properties.name: KZ Mittelbau-Dora
properties.description: Mittelbau-Dora concentration camp is where 20,000+ people were killed. The slaves at the camp were forced to dig tunnels for the production of V-1 flying bombs and V-2 rockets. The tunnels still stand so that the horror can be toured.

properties.name: Stasi-Bunker Lübschützer Teiche
properties.description: The oppressive Stasi (Ministry of State Security) built bunkers to continue their stranglehold over East German freedom in the event of nuclear war. See how the secret police intended to survive the apocalypse at the Stasi-bunker.

properties.name: Sächsisches Eisenbahnmuseum
properties.street: An d. Dresdner Bahnlinie 130c, 09131 Chemnitz, Germany
properties.description: The Saxon Railway Museum is two railway roundhouses filled with 77+ railway vehicles, including the aerodynamic VT 18.16.

properties.name: KZ Sachsenhausen
properties.description: Sachsenhausen Concentration Camp killed 10,000+ people just outside of Berlin. After the war, the Soviets NKVD used it as a gulag for 60,000+ people.

properties.name: KZ Ravensbrück
properties.description: Ravensbrück Concentration Camp was primarily for women, and 90,000+ of them were killed here in gas chambers, forced labor, death marches, murder, human experimentation, and deliberate neglect.

properties.name: U 995
properties.description: The only place in the world you can go to the beach and go on a U-boat. The WW2 era Type VIIC/41 submarine U-995 is now a museum on the beach in Laboe.

properties.name: U 11 (U-Boot, 1968)
properties.description: The U-Boo-Museum Fehmarn has the Cold War era Type 205 Submarine U-11 available for tour. This is the most modern submarine available for tour in Northern Germany.

properties.name: Internationales Feuerwehrmuseum Schwerin
properties.description: Ever wanted to know how Communist East Germany fought fires? The International Fire Department Museum Schwerin has 112+ mostly East German firefighting vehicles. There's also little fire department displays for various countries to show off their firefighting history - including England, Poland, Switzerland, Czechia, France, The Netherlands, Denmark, the Soviet Union, and Austria.

properties.name: Technik-Museum Pütnitz
properties.description: This is THE East German vehicle museum. You can drive Soviet vehicles here - including the big ones. The Pütnitz Technology Museum is stuffed into three former Soviet Air Force Hangars. It features East German vehicles in three separate halls:  a hall dedicated to Military Wheeled Vehicles, a hall of  Civil Vehicles, and a hall full of tracked military vehicles and aircraft.

properties.name: Otto-Lilienthal-Museum
properties.description: Inventing flight is really hard. Otto Lilienthal was the first person to make repeated documented glider flights that would inspire the Wright Brother's development of the first aircraft. The Otto Lilienthal Museum features replicas of all of Lilienthal's known designs.

properties.name: Nautineum Dänholm
properties.description: This maritime museum features underwater laboratories and research submarines, including the underwater laboratory Heligoland and the underwater station BAH1. They're basically underwater houses. The museum has been closed to the public since 2022 - but it will reopen eventually.

properties.name: Otus (U-Boot, 1963)
properties.description: The Cold War era Oberon-class submarine HMS Otus served in the Falklands and Gulf War, and is now a museum ship in Germany after being privately purchased.

properties.name: Oldtimer Museum Rügen
properties.description: The Oldtimer Museum is a few massive halls filled with trains, planes, and 80+ automobiles. Notably the museum features the streamlined Soviet locomotive SDC class P36, East German cars and their West German counterparts displayed side by side, and a museum dedicated to the National People's Army of East Germany .

properties.name: Miniera di Serbariu
properties.street: Grande, Miniera di Serbariu, 09013 Carbonia SU, Italy
properties.description: The 1937 Serbariu Coal Mine on Sardinia is now a museum that offers tours of the mine (reservations required). The surface of the mine reflects design patterns of the 1930s, so the whole facility has an oddly art deco feel to it.

properties.name: Segesta
properties.street: Contrada Barbaro, SR, 22, 91013 Calatafimi TP, Italy
properties.description: Legends are that the city of Segesta was founded by Trojan refugees. The ruins of the city now lay on top of a mountain, with a well preserved ancient Greek temple and theater situated on the edge of the mountainside.

properties.name: Selinunte
properties.street: Piazzale Bovio Marconi, 91022 Marinella TP, Italy
properties.description: The ancient city of Selinute has the ruins of an entire ancient Greek city and eight temples - and one of them has been reconstructed. It's kind of like running around 8 mini Parthenons with a beach view.

properties.name: Valle dei Templi
properties.street: 92100 Agrigento, Free municipal consortium of Agrigento, Italy
properties.description: A series of 7 ancient Greek temples lines the ridge of Agrigento. The mostly intact Temple of Concordia and the Temple of Hera are the standout attractions

properties.name: Parco archeologico della Neapolis
properties.street: Via Luigi Bernabò Brea, 14, 96100 Siracusa SR, Italy
properties.description: Neapolis Archaelogical Park lays in the ruins of the Corinthian city of Syracuse - the primary rival of ancient Carthage. The ruins contain a massive Greek Theater and the remains of a city crisscrossed with caves - including the famous Ear of Dionysius.

properties.name: Parco dell'Etna
properties.street: Stazione Partenza Piazzale Funivia Etna Sud, 95030 Nicolosi CT, Italy
properties.description: Mount Etna is a 11,165ft snow covered active stratovolcano on the warm Mediterranean island of Sicily. By active - they mean active - this volcano erupts nearly every year. You can hike to the top of the ash covered volcanic hellscape or hit the ski slopes.

properties.name: Paestum
properties.street: Via Magna Graecia, 919, 84047 Capaccio Paestum SA, Italy
properties.description: The ruins of the ancient Greek city of Paestum contain three fairly intact temples, an amphitheater, swimming pool, and council chamber. The ancient Greeks here were later assimilated by the nearby Romans - but the architecture remains distinctly Greek.

properties.name: Pompeii
properties.street: 80045 Pompei, Metropolitan City of Naples, Italy
properties.description: The Roman city of Pompei was buried in scorching ash clouds by the 79AD volcanic eruption of Mount Vesuvius. As a result, the city was largely preserved, and gaps in the ash allowed for the creation of plaster casts of the inhabitants as they were when they died.

properties.name: Parco nazionale del Vesuvio
properties.street: Sentiero del Gran Cono, 80056 Ercolano NA, Italy
properties.description: Mount Vesuvius National Park is centered on the 4,203ft tall active stratovolcano Vesuvius. Historically, Vesuvius has erupted and destroyed the cities surrounding it -but that hasn't stopped 600,000 people from living right next to it. At the national park, you can hike around and up to the rim of the volcano and see the smoldering crater.

properties.name: Herculaneum
properties.description: The Roman luxury seaside resort of Herculaneum was buried under the pyroclastic flow of the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79AD. Due to being buried by pyroclastic materials, the ruins of the city are better preserved than at nearby Pompei - there's still paint on the buildings. However, unlike Pompei there's no horrifying plaster casts of the dead.

properties.name: Museo nazionale ferroviario di Pietrarsa
properties.description: This is THE Italian train museum - and it's one of the few railway museums on oceanfront property. The museum is located inside a former locomotive factory and features 50+ locomotives including: a replica of the first Italian locomotive (Bayard Locomotive), a cube shaped steam locomotive, some streamlined diesel railcars, and the carriage of the Italian King.

properties.name: Galleria Borbonica
properties.street: Vico del Grottone, 3, 80132 Napoli NA, Italy
properties.description: The Bourbon Tunnel is an escape tunnel from the Royal Palace of Naples to nearby military barracks. The tunnel was later used as a bomb shelter during WW2 and contains wreckage of cars from Fascist Italy.

properties.name: Reggia di Caserta
properties.street: Piazza Carlo di Borbone, 81100 Caserta CE, Italy
properties.description: It's Neapolitan Versailles. The Royal Palace of Caserta was built as the main residence for the Kingdom of Naples (later the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies) in 1774, and is a sprawling palace and garden complex complete with massive artificial waterfall.

properties.name: Grotte di Castellana
properties.street: Piazza Franco Anelli, 70013 Castellana Grotte BA, Italy
properties.description: The Castellana Caves are characterized by a dramatic opening in the roof of the cave shining bright light upon the green stalagmites in a massive alcove.

properties.name: Soratte Bunker
properties.street: 00060 Sant Oreste, Metropolitan City of Rome Capital, Italy
properties.description: See how the Italians prepared for nuclear Armageddon at Bunker Soratte. Bunker Soratte was built in 1937 as a way to house the Italian Government and Military Command in case of wartime. During the Cold War, it transitioned to a continuity-of-government bunker in the event of nuclear war. There's 2.4km of tunnels to explore - reservations are required in advance.

properties.name: Cascata delle Marmore
properties.street: Via Strada Statale Valnerina, 05100 Terni TR, Italy
properties.description: In 271BC the Romans diverted the Velino river during land reclamation efforts, and as a result created the tallest artificial waterfall in the world at 541ft tall.

properties.name: Museo storico dell Aeronautica Militare
properties.street: Via Circumlacuale, 00062 Vigna di Valle RM, Italy
properties.description: This is THE Italian aircraft museum. The Italian Air Force Museum is located at the first Italian airport and features 80+ aircraft, including: the double-decker Savoia-Marchetti SM82, S.56 flying boat, Macchi MC202 fighter, seaplane speed record holder Macchi-Castoldi MC72, the WW1 bomber Caproni Ca.36, and the CANT Z.506 trimotor seaplane,

properties.name: Villa Adriana
properties.street: Largo Marguerite Yourcenar, 1, 00010 Tivoli RM, Italy
properties.description: Hadrian's Villa is the ruins of the palace built by Roman Emperor Hadrian in 120AD. The massive complex of 30+ buildings contains theaters, bathhouses, temples, and sculpture gardens. the entire complex is a couple square kilometers, so set aside a lot of time if you want to see everything.

properties.name: Terme di Diocleziano
properties.street: Viale Enrico de Nicola, 78, 00185 Roma RM, Italy
properties.description: The Baths of Diocletian are the largest imperial Roman bathhouses and were built in 306AD. Unlike most Roman bathhouses, the structure and roof remain intact due to being converted into two separate churches and a section of the National Roman Museum.

properties.name: Colosseo
properties.street: Piazza del Colosseo, 1, 00184 Roma RM, Italy
properties.description: The Colosseum is the largest ancient amphitheater ever built - capable of holding 80,000 spectators across its three tiers. The Colosseum was built in 80AD and was used for gladiator fights, animal hunts, public executions, and simulated sea battles.

properties.name: Circo Massimo
properties.street: 00186 Rome, Metropolitan City of Rome Capital, Italy
properties.description: Humanity has thought that racing has been awesome forever - which is why the Romans built a racetrack where 150,000+ spectators could watch chariot-racing. This is the largest stadium in all of ancient Rome, and is now just a public park.

properties.name: Pantheon (Roma)
properties.street: Piazza della Rotonda, 00186 Roma RM, Italy
properties.description: The Pantheon was built in 126AD with the largest unreinforced concrete dome ever built. The building looks great and is in a central locations - which means that it has been preserved through being in continuous use.

properties.name: Vittoriano
properties.description: The Victor Emmanuel II monument to Italian unification is also home to the Museo centrale del Risorgimento al Vittoriano (Central Museum of Italian Unification). and Sacrario delle Bandiere (Shrine of the Flags). The shrine of the flags includes flags from Italian military units, as well as the torpedo boat MAS 15 which sunk the battleship SMS Szent Istvan.

properties.name: Parco Naturale Regionale dell Antichissima Città di Sutri
properties.description: The ancient city of Sutri includes a necropolis built into the cliffside, an amphiteater, and an underground church which was once used to worship the god Mitra.

properties.name: Forte Montecchio Nord
properties.street: Via alle Torri, 8, 23823 Colico LC, Italy
properties.description: Italy built Fort Montecchio North in 1914 to defend against possible Austria-Hungary invasion through Switzerland - which never ended up happening. As a result, the fortress is the best preserved of any of the Italian border fortifications and still has its original artillery cupolas. The fort itself is located at a highpoint with a commanding view of the valley and Lake Como, so it's well worth a visit for the scenic panoramas alone.

properties.name: Diga del Vajont
properties.description: The 860ft Vajont Dam was built by the Italian government, who also concealed reports that a mountain on the lake was geologically unstable. On October 9, 1963 during the process of filling the reservoir, the side of the mountain collapsed into the lake, creating a 820ft tall wave that destroyed the towns in the valley below - killing 2,056 people. The dam and the dry reservoir below are now available for guided tours.

properties.name: Mirabilandia
properties.description: Mirabilandia is the largest theme park in Italy, featuring 10 rollercoasters, including one resembling a speeding Italian sports car, a pair of dueling motorcycle coasters, a mobius loop dueling coaster, and the tallest water coaster in the world (164ft).

properties.name: Museo della civiltà romana
properties.street: Piazza Giovanni Agnelli, 10, 00144 Roma RM, Italy
properties.description: Ever wondered what Ancient Rome looked like at its peak? The Museum of Roman Civilization has a scale model of the entire city depicting just that. There's also a bunch of sculptures and historical artifacts.

properties.name: Museo delle carrozze d epoca
properties.street: Via Andrea Millevoi, 693, 00178 Roma RM, Italy
properties.description: The Museum of Vintage Carriages contains 300+ carriages and chariots from movies filmed in Italy - which means there's a lot of Wild West carriages here.

properties.name: Museo storico della motorizzazione militare
properties.street: V.le dell Esercito, 170, 00100 Roma RM, Italy
properties.description: The Museum of Military Motorization is the only museum dedicated to military vehicles in Italy, and has 300+ trucks, cars, armored vehicles, motorcycles, and tanks. You will have to cross a military checkpoint to tour the museum - so plan ahead.

properties.name: Parco archeologico di Ostia antica
properties.street: Viale dei Romagnoli, 717, 00119 Roma RM, Italy
properties.description: The ancient Roman port city of Ostia is 150 hectares of ruins on the River Tiber. The park isn't just confined to the city of Ostia, but also includes the Castle of Julius II, the Imperial Ports of Claudius and Trajan, the Museo Dell Navi Romane, and the Necropolois of Porto Isola Sacra. All the sites are located off the same road within a 3 mile stretch.

properties.name: Castel Sant Angelo
properties.description: Wow, what a cool looking castle, I bet it's from the Renaissance era - nope - it's from 139AD. This Roman mausoleum was later turned into a fortress and prison.

properties.name: Musei Vaticani
properties.description: The Catholic Church in the Vatican City has collected around 10% of the income of 1.272 billion of its members during its existence. This means the museums here are really really nice, including the Sistine Chapel, Pinacoteca Vaticana art museum, Collection of Modern Religious Arts, Museo Pio-Clementino and Museo Chiaramonti sculpture museums, Museo Gregoriano Etrusco and Museo Gregorizano Egiziano museum of Etruscan and Egyptian artifacts, and the Vatican Historical Museum.

properties.name: Piazza dei Miracoli
properties.street: Piazza del Duomo, 56126 Pisa PI, Italy
properties.description: The Piazza del Duomo (now known as Piazza dei Miracoli) is home to the famous Leaning Tower of Pisa. After you get your obligatory photograph of you holding up the leaning tower, check out the architecture and art of the Pisa Cathedral, Pisa Baptistery, Camposanto Monumentale, Museo dell'Opea del Duomo, and Museo dell Sinopie located adjacent.

properties.name: Museo delle navi antiche di Pisa
properties.street: Lungarno Ranieri Simonelli, 16, 56126 Pisa PI, Italy
properties.description: The Museum of Ancient Ships contains the wreckage and reproductions of Roman ships that once sailed the Arno river. If you are expecting massive rowing vessels, this isn't it - the Romans had modest sailing ships for river based trade.

properties.name: Galata Museo del Mare
properties.street: Calata Ansaldo De Mari, 1, 16126 Genova GE, Italy
properties.description: The Museum of the Sea in Genoa contains the Cold War era Sauro-class submarine Nazrio Sauro, a reproduction of the brigatine Anna, and various exhibits about Italian maritime history.

properties.name: Museo per la Memoria di Ustica
properties.street: Via di Saliceto, 3/22, 40128 Bologna BO, Italy
properties.description: On June 27, 1980 Itavia Flight 870 crashed into the ocean killing all onboard - with the cause of the crash still uncertain. The museum displays the wreckage of the aircraft meticulously put back together.

properties.name: Museo Ferruccio Lamborghini
properties.street: SP4, 40050 Casette di Funo BO, Italy
properties.description: Successful tractor manufacturer Ferrucio Lamborghini complained to Enzo Ferrari about Ferrari's quality and aftermarket service - which led to Ferrari refusing to sell Lamborghini any other cars. Lamborghini decided to make his own sports car company out of spite. The Ferrucio Lamborghibi Museum contains every production vehicle made by Lamborghini - including the tractors, sports cars, helicopter, and boats.

properties.name: Cattedrale di Santa Maria del Fiore
properties.street: Piazza del Duomo, 50122 Firenze FI, Italy
properties.description: It's a really pretty green, white, and pink marble building. The dome of Cattedrale di Santa Maria del Fiore is the largest masonry dome ever constructed, and the lavish gothic decorations are a triumph of Italian renaissance paintings, sculpture, and architecture.

properties.name: Palazzo Pitti
properties.street: Piazza de' Pitti, 1, 50125 Firenze FI, Italy
properties.description: Pitti Palace was the principal palace of the ruling Medici family of the Grand Duchy of Tuscany from 1589-1860, and is now a museum complex featuring: the Palatine Gallery, Carriages museum, Russian Icons Museum, Porceilain Museum, Gallery of Modern Art, Treasury of the Grand Dukes, and Royal Apartments, and Boboli Gardens.

properties.name: Galleria degli Uffizi
properties.street: Piazzale degli Uffizi, 6, 50122 Firenze FI, Italy
properties.description: The Uffizi art gallery contains the Renaissance art collection of the House of Medici - the family that commissioned all the really cool Renaissance art. Botticelli's The Birth of Venus is located here.

properties.name: Galleria dell Accademia
properties.description: The Gallery of Academy of Florence has a large number of sculptures by Michelangelo - including the David featuring its freakishly large hands. There's also a lot of paintings and sculptures by other artists. You will need to book your ticket ahead of time - plan ahead.

properties.name: Museo Stibbert
properties.street: Via Federico Stibbert, 26, 50134 Firenze FI, Italy
properties.description: This is THE armor museum. Frederick Stibbert hoarded 16,000 pieces of antique armor from Europe, Asia, the Middle East, and gifted his collection to the city of Florence in 1906.

properties.name: Diga del Gleno
properties.street: Lago del Gleno, 24020 Vilminore di Scalve BG, Italy
properties.description: Hike in the scenic corpse of the Gleno Dam in the Alps, and see the much smaller newer dam built in the middle of the wreckage. The Gleno Dam failed on October 22, 1923 due to faulty construction, killing 356 people - but now it's a beautiful hike.

properties.name: Cascate del Serio
properties.description: The 1000ft tall Serio Falls are the second tallest waterfalls in Italy, and pour out of a reservoir down a mountainside into the river valley below. Like most European parks, you'll have to hike to see anything good.

properties.name: Museo Fisogni
properties.street: Via Giacomo Bianchi, 25b, 21049 Tradate VA, Italy
properties.description: The Fisogni Museum of the Service Station features 8,000 gas pumps, signs, and other gas station memorabilia. It's just room after room of gas pumps. If electric cars ever come to dominate the market this museum will become even more nostalgic.

properties.name: Volandia
properties.street: Via per Tornavento, 15, 21019 Somma Lombardo VA, Italy
properties.description: Volandia is the largest aeronautical museum in Italy featuring 100+ aircraft including the Italian equivalent of Airforce One. There's also 76+ cars here and some trains.

properties.name: Museo nazionale della scienza e della tecnologia Leonardo da Vinci
properties.street: Via San Vittore, 21, 20123 Milano MI, Italy
properties.description: The Leonardo da Vinci Science and Technology museum is a massive museum of Italian technology, including: the Cold War era Toti-class submarine Enrico Toti, the training ship Ebe, the deck of the transatlantic passenger ship SS Conte Biancamano, a replica of the ESA rocket Vega, the inventions of Leonardo da Vinci, 18 locomotives, the Red Tent used by the survivors of the airship Italia crash in the arctic, and multiple aircraft.

properties.name: Castello Sforzesco
properties.description: Sforza Castle was the primary fortification for the city of Milan, and is now a museum complex featuring: the Art Gallery of Sfroza Castle, Museum of Prehistory, Egyptian Museum, Museum of Ancient Art, Museum of Musical Instruments, Museum of Furniture and Wood Sculptures, Civic Collections of Applied Art, Extra-European Collection, etc. It's a big castle.

properties.name: Forte di Bard
properties.street: Via Vittorio Emanuele II, 11020 Bard AO, Italy
properties.description: Fort Bard stands resolute on a hill in the middle of Aosta Valley where it holds the Museum of the Alps. The fort is in an extremely strong defensive position, 400 soldiers were able to hold back 40,000 French troops for two weeks in 1800. Napoleon was so annoyed by the fort's ability to halt his army that he razed it - the modern fort is an 1830s reconstruction.

properties.name: Museo Nazionale dell'Automobile
properties.street: Corso Unità d'Italia, 40, 10126 Torino TO, Italy
properties.description: Turin is the center of the Italian automotive industry, so the National Automobile Museum and its 200+ cars are located here. The museum follows the history of car development in Italy from 1769-present, including: Cugnot's 1769 self propelled steam vehicle, and far too many Italian sports cars.

properties.name: Reggia di Venaria Reale
properties.street: Piazza della Repubblica, 4, 10078 Venaria Reale TO, Italy
properties.description: The Palace of Venaria was intended to be a luxury palace for the House of Savoy - the dynasty that led the tiny county of Savoy into uniting Italy. The palace and gardens are home to an art museum, carriage collection, and royal barge.

properties.name: Palazzo Reale (Torino)
properties.description: The Royal Palace of Turin was the seat of power for the House of Savoy as it consolidated its power from the county of Savoy into unified Italy. The palace in the middle of Turin is now a museum complex: including: the Musei Reali, Royal Armory, and Museo di Antichita di Torino.

properties.name: Stellantis Heritage
properties.street: Ingresso 31, Via Plava, 80, 10135 Torino TO, Italy
properties.description: This is THE Fiat museum. Stellantis (totally not Fiat wearing the skin of Citroen, Peugeot, Opel, and Chrysler) has a heritage hub where they keep 300+ of only the Italian vehicles they are proud to have made.

properties.name: Museo storico navale
properties.street: Riva S. Biasio, 2148, 30122 Venezia VE, Italy
properties.description: The Republic of Venice was a historical naval power located on an impregnable island in the Venetian lagoon. The Naval Historical Museum of Venice follows Venetian naval history and also possesses gondolas, luxury barges, and steamboats in its Ship Pavillion. Located a short distance away is the Cold War era Toti-class submarine Enrico Dandolo in the middle of the Venice arsenal. Reserve tickets ahead of time - tourists love Venice.

properties.name: Piazza San Marco
properties.street: P.za San Marco, 30100 Venezia VE, Italy
properties.description: Piazza San Marco is the architectural center of Venice, featuring the renaissance architecture of the Doge's Palace, the Campanile di San Marco tower, and Basilica di San Marco cathedral. Reserve tickets ahead of time, Venice is popular.

properties.name: Museo delle forze armate 1914-1945
properties.street: Via del Lavoro, 66, 36075 Montecchio Maggiore VI, Italy
properties.description: This Italian Military History museum and its 30+ vehicles is dedicated to the period 1914-1945. More importantly, the museum built a reconstruction of the Fiat 2000 - the first Italian tank.

properties.name: Museo Nicolis
properties.street: V.le Postumia, 71, 37069 Villafranca di Verona VR, Italy
properties.description: Entrepreneur Luciano Nicholis began hoarding 135+ cars, 114+ motorcycles, 108+ bicycles, 3 airplanes, 39+ musical instruments, 500+ cameras, 80+ typewriters, and other odds and ends until he had his own museum.

properties.name: Grotta Gigante
properties.street: Borgo Grotta Gigante, 42 / A, 34010 Sgonico TS, Italy
properties.description: Grotta Gigante is unique among caves in that it's just one really giant hall - at 351ft high and 430ft wide. The walls are covered in stalagmites and stalactites, so it's pretty to look at too.

properties.name: Parco naturale Paneveggio - Pale di San Martino
properties.street: Località Castelpietra, 2, 38054 Primiero San Martino di Castrozza TN, Italy
properties.description: Paneveggio-Pale di San Martino Natural Park encompasses the Dolomites, and unlike some of the other Italian parks there's a road that passes straight through the prettiest parts: Strada Statale 50 which goes over the mountain from San Martinto to Paneveggio. There's also hiking and skiing.

properties.name: Ġgantija
properties.street: Triq John Otto Bayer, Ix-Xagħra, Malta
properties.description: This megalithic temple complex was built five millennium ago around 3600BC. If some of the oldest sites known to mankind don't impress you, I don't know what will.

properties.name: Popeye Village
properties.description: The film set from the 1980 live action adaptation of Popeye has been turned into a local attraction - it's like a 1930s cartoon came to life.

properties.name: Ħaġar Qim
properties.street: Triq Ħaġar Qim Qrendi QRD, Malta
properties.description: The Ħaġar Qim and Mnajdra megalithic complexes were constructed sometime around 3400BC, making them some of the oldest known architecture. The ruins are literally prehistoric - there is no written history of why and when they were built.

properties.name: Lascaris War Rooms
properties.description: Malta occupies a strategic chokepoint in the Mediterranean, which meant during WW2 it got bombed a lot. The Lascaris War Rooms were built as bunkers to maintain operations during the frequent bombing of Malta, later being transformed into command centers during the Cold War.

properties.name: Grandmaster's Palace, Valletta
properties.description: The Knights Hospitaller of Saint John of Jerusalem were Crusaders who ruled over Malta from 1530-1798. The Palace Armoury and the Palace State Rooms are now museums available for tour where you can see the art and armor of the Knights Hospitaller.

properties.name: Cheddar Gorge
properties.street: The Cliffs, Cheddar BS27 3QF, United Kingdom
properties.description: The 450ft tall Cheddar Gorge is rife with caves and hiking. There's a road that winds through the narrow gorge itself, and Gough's Cave and Cox's Cave to see the underground where 9,000+ year old human remains were found. The gorge is only a mile long, so it's a pretty doable hike for even amateurs.

properties.name: Haynes International Motor Museum
properties.description: The Haynes International Motor Museum has 328+ cars and 49+ motorcycles from British automotive history, including a strong selection Austin, Morris, and Triumph vehicles. Notably there is a room filled entirely with red sports cars

properties.name: VerhalenArk
properties.description: Johan Huibers built a replica of the Biblical Noah's Ark on top of a steel barge. The ark is now full of unnerving wooden puppets depicting biblical scenes.

properties.name: Marinemuseum (Den Helder)
properties.description: The Netherlands has always had a strong maritime tradition - leading to the formation of a global trade empire and sparring with other European naval powers. The Navy Museum follows the history of the Dutch Royal Navy, and includes the 1868 ramship Schorpioen, the 1937 minesweeper Abraham Crijnssen which survived WW2 in the Pacific by disguising itself as an island,  the Cold War era Dolfijn-class submarine Tonijn, the bridge of the frigate De Ruyter. Docked nearby is the Hr.Ms. Bonaire (1877) - it's not part of the museum, but it's right next to it.

properties.name: Nationaal Militair Museum
properties.description: The National Military Museum is the museum for the Dutch Army and Air Force. It's not the largest museum for vehicles, but it is for the Dutch military. You can ride around in a jeep or half-track here.

properties.name: Museum Speelklok
properties.description: It's a museum full of delightful tiny little Dutch automated music machines and automatons. These machines are the ones that aren't trying to take your job.

properties.name: Louwman Museum
properties.description: The Louwman family has been hoarding historic vehicles since 1934 and now have 275+ cars; with a wide selection from defunct Dutch car manufacturers.

properties.name: Hr.Ms. Buffel (1868)
properties.description: Hellevoetsluis in the Netherlands is where the Dutch send the museum ships they don't love enough to wait out their days until the Dutch people smile upon them again. The 1868 Ram ship Buffel is one of the oldest ships afloat globally, and is also docked next to the Lightship 12 Noord Hinder and the minesweeper AMS 60 Bernisse.

properties.name: Luchtvaartmuseum Aviodrome
properties.description: In the famous words of KLM captain Jacob Velhuzen van Zanten "We're Going". The Netherlands used to have an aviation industry until Fokker went bankrupt. See 83+ aircraft, including a KLM 747 like the one that crashed into another 747 at Tenerife in 1977.

properties.name: DAF Museum
properties.description: The Netherlands used to have its own automotive and truck manufacturer DAF until it was bought by Volvo and Paccar. Come and see a long history of funny looking Dutch car and truck prototypes and production models.

properties.name: Fort Eben-Emael
properties.description: After their fortifications were overwhelmed by the invading Germans in WW1, the Belgians decided to build bigger fortifications to stop another German invasion - it didn't work. Fort Eben-Emael was where the Nazis broke through the Belgian defensive lines by surprise paratrooper attack. Now you can tour the mostly underground fortress and maybe learn a lesson about the futility of fixed defenses in modern warfare.

properties.name: Bastogne Barracks
properties.description: During WW2 a surprise German offensive tried and failed to capture the strategic logistics town of Bastogne despite a 6-day siege and outnumbering American forces 5:1. The Bastogne Barracks possesses mechanized warfare vehicles from both sides of WW2. This isn't the biggest museum of the Battle of Bastogne, but it's the one with more vehicles.

properties.name: Bois du Cazier
properties.description: Usually when there's a mining disaster that kills 262 people, that coal mine isn't turned into a museum.

properties.name: Champ de bataille de Waterloo
properties.description: Somehow, Napoleon returned - and the nations of Europe scrambled to send armies to defeat him again. At Waterloo, the French army very nearly overwhelmed combined British and German forces, but was ultimately defeated in the second largest battle of the Napoleonic Wars. The battlefield is fairly unchanged - it's still some farmer's fields where 51,000 people became casualties.

properties.name: Walibi Belgium
properties.description: Walibi Belgium is one of the largest amusement parks in Belgium, and has some inspired ride design choices - such as putting a Schwarzkopf shuttle loop indoors, a Belgian version of Big Thunder Mountain Railroad, and an edgy punk rock kangaroo as a mascot.

properties.name: Mahymobiles
properties.description: Garage owner Ghislain Mahy hoarded so many cars his massive collection is split between Mahymobiles and Autoworld. There are 300+ vehicles alone at Mahymobiles, it's row after row of cars.

properties.name: Passchendaele Museum
properties.description: WW1 British military command decided that charging the machine guns head on would end the war this time for sure - 700,000 casualties disagreed. Record rainfall turned the battlefield into a muddy morass where if you found yourself stuck - you simply disappeared into the bottom of the muck with the rest of the corpses. Now you can see what that would have been like at the Passchendaele Museum.

properties.name: Commandobunker van Kemmel
properties.description: During the Cold War Belgium built a bunker to continue command of the military in the event of nuclear attack or Soviet invasion. What's nice about this bunker is it really looked like the stereotype of what you'd expect a secret military bunker to look like.

properties.name: Parc du Cinquantenaire
properties.description: This is THE Belgian museum center. Parc du Cinquantenaire was developed as an exposition for the 50th anniversary of Belgian independence, then developed further for the Brussels International Exposition of 1897. As a result the park is now a massive museum complex featuring: the Royal Museum of Art and History; the 300+ vehicles of Autoworld; and the tanks, boats, artillery pieces, and 100+ aircraft of the Royal Museum of the Armed Forces and Military History.

properties.name: Train World
properties.description: The Schaerbeek railway station is now a railway museum, and yeah there's only 22 trains here, but they're really cool looking trains. When you see the streamlined SNCB Type 12 you'll understand.

properties.name: Koninklijk Domein van Laken
properties.street: Av. du Parc Royal 61, 1020 Bruxelles, Belgium
properties.description: The Royal Domain of Laeken is a large public park featuring the Palace of Laeken where Belgian royalty still reside, Royal Greenhouses of Laeken, English gardens, Japanese gardens, and the Museums of the Far East (which will reopen someday).

properties.name: Bayeux Tapestry
properties.description: William the Conqueror conquered England in 1066, and admirers made a 70ft long blanket about how cool he was.

properties.name: Musée du débarquement
properties.street: Place du 6 Juin, 14 Pl. du Six Juin 1944, 14117 Arromanches-les-Bains, France
properties.description: Operation Overlord during WW2 was the largest naval invasion ever, storming beachheads and landing literally millions of soldiers onto floating artificial harbors. The Landing Museum at Arromanches sits directly on Gold Beach and preserves the ruins of the artificial Mulberry Harbors.

properties.name: La Cité de la Mer
properties.street: All. du Président Menut, 50100 Cherbourg-en-Cotentin, France
properties.description: This is THE French submarine museum. The Art Deco transatlantic ferry terminal at Cherbourg has been transformed into a maritime museum which is now full of submarines, including: the first French nuclear ballistic missile submarine Redoutable; the bathyscaphe Archimedes, five Submarines made by Comex; and replicas of the exploration submarines Alvin, Mir Nautilus, and Bathysphere.

properties.name: Le Mont-Saint-Michel
properties.description: The island Mont-Saint-Michel is only accessible from the mainland at low tide, making it an ideal defensive position for an abbey. More importantly, it looks really pretty.

properties.name: Cité des télécoms
properties.description: Before satellite communication, this massive antenna was built to transmit television signals across the Atlantic. There's also a nice telecommunications museums accompanying it with a semaphore tower.

properties.name: Base sous-marine de Lorient
properties.street: Tour Davis - Base de Sous Marins de Keroman, 56100 Lorient, France
properties.description: During WW2 the Nazis built nearly indestructible concrete submarine pens, which the French took over. Now the concrete bunker houses the Cold War era Daphné-class submarine Flore for tour.

properties.name: Manoir de l automobile
properties.street: 4 Rue de la Cour Neuve, 35550 Lohéac, France
properties.description: French magazine publisher Michel Hommel began collecting 400+ vehicles then put them in his 17th century manor and racing circuit.

properties.name: Base sous-marine de Saint-Nazaire
properties.street: 9 Bd de la Légion d'Honneur, 44600 Saint-Nazaire, France
properties.description: During WW2 the Nazis built a massive concrete bunker for their submarines in St. Nazaire. Now you can tour the submarine pens,the Cold War era Narval-class submarine Espadon, or go to the Escal'Atlantic museum which features a replica of a French transatlantic passenger ship.

properties.name: Batterie Todt
properties.street: Batterie Todt, hameau de Haringzelle, 566 route du musée, 62179 Audinghen, France
properties.description: After defeating the French in WW2, the Nazis embarked on building a line of fortifications to prevent naval invasions called the Atlantic Wall. The artillery Batterie Todt was intended to dominate the Strait of Dover to enable an invasion of Britain. The artillery battery and a rail gun are now available at the Museum of the Atlantic Wall at Batterie Todt.

properties.name: La Coupole (France)
properties.description: During WW2 the Nazis built the world's first underground missile silo to launch V-2 rockets at England on an industrial scale. The Allies bombed it before it could ever become operational.  Now you can tour what is pretty much a real life James Bond villain lair.

properties.name: Mémorial de Vimy
properties.street: Route départementale 55, Chem. des Canadiens, 62580 Givenchy-en-Gohelle, France
properties.description: During WW1 all four divisions of the Canadian expeditionary force captured Vimy Ridge during the Battle of Arras at the cost of 10,000+ casualties. The ridge is the site of the memorial, and the Vimy Ridge Visitor Educate Centre is located in the woods where trenches and craters still lay. Stay on the footpaths, the ground is still full of exploded shells.

properties.name: Musée Somme 1916
properties.description: During the Battle of the Somme in 1916, 1+ million men were turned into casualties in just 4 months - all to move the front line 10km towards Berlin. Now, WW2 air raid shelters have been turned into replicas of the battlefield at the Somme Museum 1916. The battlefield lays to the east of the town, which is now farmer's fields with the occasional crater and cemetery.

properties.name: Centre historique minier de Lewarde
properties.street: Fosse Delloye, Rue d'Erchin, 59287 Lewarde, France
properties.description: Unlike most European coal mines, they actually let you go into the tunnels at the 1927 Delloye pit of the Lewarde Mining Historic Center.

properties.name: Clairière de l Armistice
properties.description: World War I ended here in this train car. By the end of 1918 Germany was starving due to the Entente blockade. Additionally the German military was retreating, socialists had overthrown the monarchy, Communist revolutionaries were attempting a coup back in Berlin, and German ally Austria-Hungary had disintegrated. The French were predictably angry about being invaded and having 1.73 million of their countrymen dead, and 4.26 million wounded - and demanded and received the total dismantling of the German military in exchange for the idea that the blockade might be lifted after a final peace treaty in Paris.

properties.name: Musée national de la Voiture et du Tourisme
properties.street: Pl. du Général de Gaulle, 60200 Compiègne, France
properties.description: Louis XV commissioned his own royal residence in Compiègne in 1751,  it was finished in 1788, seized during the French revolution in 1789, and restored by Napoleon in 1807. Now it's home to the 100+ carriages and 30+ vehicles of the National Car and Tourism Museum - including the record setting La Jamais Contente - the fastest car in the world in 1899.

properties.name: Maillé-Brézé (D627)
properties.street: Quai de la Fosse, 44000 Nantes, France
properties.description: The Cold War era T 47-class destroyer Maillé-Brézé is now a museum ship in Nantes. This is one of the few French naval surface vessels available for tour.

properties.name: Musée des 24 Heures du Mans
properties.street: 9 Pl. Luigi Chinetti, 72100 Le Mans, France
properties.description: The 24 Hours of Le Mans is the oldest endurance motorsport race in the world, and this museum of 100+ cars is located right on the racing circuit.

properties.name: Musée automobile de Vendée
properties.street: D949 Avenue des Sables, 85440 Talmont-Saint-Hilaire, France
properties.description: 160+ automobiles are kept in a building with a giant tire archway. Notably there are a number of concept cars.

properties.name: Fort du Portalet
properties.description: Fort du Portalet overlooks a dramatic valley in the Pyrenees, and was built in 1842 to guard against incursions from Spain. The scenic fort was later used  by the Nazis to intern important French officials, and again by the 4th Republic as a prison for Nazi collaborators like Pétain. Tours by reservation only, so plan ahead.

properties.name: Grotte de La Verna
properties.description: This cave is like standing inside of a stadium. La Verna cave is the largest showcave cave in the world, with an 820ft diameter and 636ft height. There's also a few waterfalls inside the cave itself. Make sure to book tours ahead of time.

properties.name: Centre de la mémoire d'Oradour
properties.description: The Nazis slaughtered every civilian in Ouradour-sur-Glane as a punitive measure for resistance in the area. The ruins of the village have been left as they were on the day that 642 people were killed there.

properties.name: Tumulus de Bougon
properties.description: In 4800 BC the neolithic people of France built this necropolis. You can enter the tumulus here - or at least their reconstructions.

properties.name: Musée maritime de La Rochelle
properties.street: Pl. Bernard Moitessier, 17000 La Rochelle, France
properties.description: Before weather satellites, meteorological ships were moored in the ocean to collect weather information. At the La Rochelle maritime museum you can tour the meteorological ship France I, the fishing trawler Angoumois, and the tugboat Saint-Gilles.

properties.name: Musée des Blindés
properties.description: This is THE French tank museum. Featuring 250+ armored vehicles - many of which still run. There's just about every French tank ever made here, including the ARL 44, B1 BIS, Saint-Chamond, Schneider CA-1, and AMX-30 equipped with a nuclear missile. There's also German, British, American, and Soviet tanks here as well.

properties.name: Musée Automobile Reims-Champagne
properties.description: This car museum stands out due to its 120+ pedal car collection. There's also 160+ cars, 90+ motorcycles, and 7,000+ miniature cars.

properties.name: Fort de la Pompelle
properties.street: RD 944, , route de Châlons-en-Champagne, 51500 Puisieulx, France
properties.description: Fort de la Pompelle was a consistent part of the front lines of WW1 and was vigorously bombarded from the beginning of the war until its end.

properties.name: Musée Guerre et Paix en Ardennes
properties.description: It wouldn't be a German invasion of France without the occupation of the Ardennes. The Museum of War and Peace in the Ardennes documents the Franco-Prussian War, WW1, and WW2.

properties.name: Fort de Douaumont
properties.description: Fort Douaumont looks pockmarked and lumpy because 10 million artillery shells were fired around it during the Battle of Verdun in WW1, leaving the landscape around it permanently uninhabitable due to the amount of unexploded ordinance. There were 750,000 casualties during the 9 month Battle of Verdun, and now you can tour the fort where a lot of them happened. You will need to reserve your ticket to the fort online.

properties.name: MuséoParc Alésia
properties.street: 1 Route des trois Ormeaux, 21150 Alise-Sainte-Reine, France
properties.description: In 52BC Julius Caesar and his 75,000 strong Roman legions surrounded and besieged a 170,000 strong Gallic army, only to be surrounded themselves by a 300,000 strong Gallic army. Caesar built fortifications to guard against the armies outside and inside and defeated both forces - leading to complete Roman annexation of Gaul. Now you can see reconstructions of the fortifications and learn about how France became Roman.

properties.name: Ouvrage de Schœnenbourg
properties.street: Rue Commandant Martial Reynier, 67250 Hunspach, France
properties.description: After WW1, France built a series of impervious underground interconnected fortifications on its border with Germany, forcing the Germans to attack through areas that the French could quickly react to. During WW2, the Nazis attacked through the Ardennes, and allied forces did not react quickly enough. Now you can tour one of the fortresses of the Maginot line at Schœnenbourg and see the retractable turrets and bunkers.

properties.name: Ouvrage du Four-à-Chaux
properties.street: D65 GPS lat.48.993304 long, 7.793876, 67510 Lembach, France
properties.description: Ouvrage Four-à-Chaux is another impressive fort of the Maginot line which saw battle during WW2 and continued service during the Cold War.

properties.name: Ouvrage du Simserhof
properties.description: Simserhof is another large fortress in the Maginot Line, this is one of the better cared for fortresses. You will likely need a ticket ahead of time.

properties.name: Ouvrage Michelsberg
properties.street: Lorraine, Rte de Dalstein, 57320 Ébersviller, France
properties.description: Ouvrage Michelsberg is another large work in the Maginot Line of fortresses designed to protect against German invasion. The tunnels here are nearly 1km long.

properties.name: Ouvrage du Hackenberg
properties.description: Yeah, it's another gros ourvrage in the Maginot Line designed to protect France from Germany, but this one still has a working underground train you can ride on. Hackenberg saw fighting during 1940 and 1944, and was used as a factory by the Nazis. Hackenberg escape deterioration due to quickly being preserved following abandonment in 1970.

properties.name: Ouvrage de Fermont
properties.description: Ouvrage de Fermont is an underground fortress in the Maginot Line designed to protect France from Germany during the interwar period. This fortress still has their underground train running and has a hiking trail for the above ground section of the fortress. You will need to reserve a tour online ahead of time.

properties.name: Écomusée des mines de fer de Lorraine
properties.description: The iron mines at Neufchef have been active since 1820, but the mining museum here is themed to the work done during the 1950s, giving the location a retro-futuristic aesthetic. Yes you can go underground to the mining tunnels here.

properties.name: Musée militaire Park France
properties.description: This is the #2 military museum in France, but the 120+ vehicles here are focused on WW2 only - and they're all kinda just in a row in one big room.

properties.name: KZ Natzweiler-Struthof
properties.street: Mémorial du camp de concentration de Natzweiler-Struthof D130, 67130 Natzwiller, France
properties.description: The Nazis put resisters in its occupied territories into Natzweiler-Struthof concentration camp, where they killed 22,000 of them in death marches, forced labor, executions, and human experimentation.

properties.name: Tellure (musée)
properties.description: This silver mine was started in 1520, and the unsafe looking tunnels you can tour reflect that.

properties.name: Cité de l Automobile
properties.street: 17 Rue de la Mertzau, 68100 Mulhouse, France
properties.description: This is THE French automobile museum. The National Museum of the Automobile has 400+ vehicles, with a notably large selection of Bugattis.

properties.name: Cité du Train
properties.street: 2 Rue Alfred de Glehn, 68200 Mulhouse, France
properties.description: This is THE French train museum. Train City follows French railway development and features 110+ trains and 70+ railcars.

properties.name: Mine de Maron Val-de-Fer
properties.street: Rue du Val de Fer, 54230 Neuves-Maisons, France
properties.description: This 1874 French iron mine also served as a military headquarters during WW1. Yes you can tour the mine here and it's just as unnerving as mines are supposed to look.

properties.name: Parc naturel régional du Doubs Horloger
properties.description: The vertical cliffs of the Doubs River Gorge divides Switzerland from France. The gorge features waterfalls such as Saut du Doubs and Consolation.

properties.name: Citadelle de Besançon
properties.street: 99 Rue des Fusillés de la Résistance, 25000 Besançon, France
properties.description: Would it be cool to go to a zoo inside of a 1683 Fortress on top of a mountain? Yes, yes it would. The Citadelle of Bescanson is a museum complex which features the Museum of Resistance and Deportation, the Comtois Museum, and the Zoological Gardens. The views from the top are quite nice.

properties.name: Château de Savigny-lès-Beaune
properties.street: Chateau de Savigny, Rue Général Leclerc, 21420 Savigny-lès-Beaune, France
properties.description: Winemaker and Abarth rally car driver Michel Pont began hoarding wine presses, 25+ tractors, 100+ aircraft, 35+ racecars, 20+ firetrucks,  250+ motorcycles, and 8,000 scale models in a 14th century castle. There's also a hovercraft here.

properties.name: Musée de la mine de La Machine
properties.street: 1 Av. de la République, 58260 La Machine, France
properties.description: The La Machine Mining Museum lets you tour the coal mining galleries of the 1863 Glénons Pit. There's no lights in this mine except for the ones you bring, so stay on the path.

properties.name: Musée de la mine de Blanzy
properties.street: 34 Rue du Bois Clair, 71450 Blanzy, France
properties.description: The Blanzy Mining Museum has a variety of historical coal mining equipment within the mine itself since the mine ran from 1761-1979. The mining tunnels here are illuminated - which is safer, but slightly less awesome.

properties.name: Barrage de Malpasset
properties.street: Parking départ excursion du barrage de Malpasset 83600 Fréjus, France
properties.description: Walk through and climb over the wreckage of a French dam and the flood scoured valley downstream. The 1952 Malpasset Dam failed on December 2, 1959, killing 423 people - so now it's a hiking trail.

properties.name: Musée de l Artillerie
properties.street: 1580 Av. de la Grande Armée, 83300 Draguignan, France
properties.description: Draguignan is the location of the French Artillery School where the French military trains its artillery operators. The Artillery Museum has 50+ historical artillery pieces - it's not the biggest artillery museum, but it is the most French.

properties.name: Parc naturel régional du Verdon
properties.description: The 700 meter (~2300ft) deep Verdon Gorge is the star of Verdon Regional Park. You can hike, kayak, or drive through the gorge along D952, or along the rim on D71.

properties.name: Parc national des Calanques
properties.description: Calanques National Park is where the jagged white rocks form scenic coves and beaches on the Mediterranean. Yes you can hike most of it, even the spines of Rocher des Goudes.

properties.name: Colorado provençal
properties.description: The ref buttes and fairy chimneys in Provencal Colorado looks like the badlands of the American Southwest, but is instead in the green forests of Southern France.

properties.name: Musée de la Révolution française
properties.description: The 1789 French Revolution ended feudalism and the power of the church over state in Western Europe - achieving what the British had already figured out in 1651. The Château de Vizille was where the Assembly of Vizille demanded the convocation of the Estates-General with the Third Estate being granted double the vote of the Clergy and Nobility - meaning that the people would finally have domination over the nobility instead of the other way around.

properties.name: Le Compa, le musée de l'agriculture
properties.street: Pont de Mainvilliers 28000 Chartres, 1 Rue de la République, 28300 Mainvilliers, France
properties.description: This is THE French tractor museum - featuring 60+ tractors. Learn how French agriculture went from people in fields to fancy machinery - they even have a life sized tractor made out of legos.

properties.name: Musée Maurice Dufresne
properties.description: Scrap dealer Maurice Dufresne started saving things he thought ought to be in a museum - then made his own museum filled with 3,000 machines - including a portable guillotine.

properties.name: Musée de automobile Henri-Malartre
properties.description: Automobile wrecker Henri Malartre refused to scrap models he found to be historically interesting - and began amassing a collection in a barn, and later transitioned the collection into a hilltop Chateau overlooking Lyon.

properties.name: Musée Baster - Musée de la moto
properties.description: The Baster Motorcycle Museum has 400+ two wheeled vehicles, they're all just kinda piled together in one room.

properties.name: Parc naturel régional des Volcans d'Auvergne
properties.description: Southern France used to be an active volcanic area including the extinct Cantal stratovolcano. Now you can roam atop and through volcanic cinders and jagged peaks like those at Puy de Sancy. There's even a roman temple on top of Puy de Dome.

properties.name: Grottes de Jonas
properties.description: Celts dug a fortress into the cliffs of the Jonas volcano. On some days there are character actors filling the caves. Tours by reservation only - plan ahead.

properties.name: Musée de la Grande Guerre du pays de Meaux
properties.description: The 1914 German offensive through Belgium reached the outskirts of Paris - but was halted by the French army at the Battle of the Marne near this museum in Meaux. The Museum of the Great War is the biggest WW1 museum in Europe, and includes little trenches where you can run around and watch character actors pretend they're having a terrible time in WW1.

properties.name: Château de Versailles
properties.description: Until the industrial revolution, France was the strongest and richest nation in Europe- and Versailles was the palace where all the money and power went.  After nearly being overthrown by the nobility as a child, French King Louis XIV built a gilded cage for the nobility to distract them with continuous pageantry - and keep them away from their bases of power. Versailles is also where the Third Estate seized power from the nobility and the clergy during the French Revolution in 1789, where the German states created the German Empire in 1871, and where the German Empire was destroyed by the Treaty of Versailles in 1919. Versailles is massive- the grounds are nearly 2 miles across with multiple palaces, and a fake village where the nobility could pretend to be poor in a controlled environment.

properties.name: Musée de l'air et de l'espace
properties.street: Aéroport de Paris-Le Bourget, 93352 Le Bourget, France
properties.description: This is THE French air museum, featuring 150+ airplanes from France's development of flight located inside the 1930s Art Deco terminal of Le Bourget Airport. This is the museum where all of France's experimental aircraft and rockets end up. Featuring 1880s gliders, the first airships to ever complete a circuit, a Caudron G.4, experimental ramjet aircraft, two Concordes, an A380, and various French rockets.

properties.name: Cité des sciences et de l'industrie
properties.description: The City of Science and Industry is more of a science museum for kids than an industry museum, it's also home to the Cold War era Aréthuse-class submarine Argonaute.

properties.name: Musée des Arts et Métiers
properties.description: The 710AD Priory of Saint-Martin-des-Champs has been turned into the Museum of Arts and Crafts, featuring demonstrations of famous French inventions such as: the Foucault pendulum which proved Earth's rotation, the 1897 steam powered aircraft Avion III (which didn't fly, but it looks cool), Pascal's mechanical calculator, the Fardier de Cugnot (the first steam powered vehicle ever built from 1771), and the first aircraft to cross the English channel.

properties.name: Musée du Louvre
properties.description: This is THE French art museum. The Louvre Museum is best known for being home of the Mona Lisa, but it's also a former Royal Palace for the French Monarchy stuffed with the very best art money could buy and an Empire could loot. This includes Egyptian antiquities such as the Great Sphinx of Tanis, Assyrian Lamasu, Renaissance paintings, and Greek sculptures.

properties.name: Hôtel des Invalides
properties.description: Hôtel des Invalides was created as a home for injured soldiers in 1670, but is now a museum complex including: the Tomb of Napoleon, the museum of the French Army (Musée de l'Armée) , Museum of Military Models (Musée des Plans-reliefs), Charles de Gaulle Museum (Historial Charles de Gaulle), and Museum of the Liberation (Musée de l'ordre de la Libération).

properties.name: Tour Eiffel
properties.description: The Eiffel Tower was built as the tallest human-made structure in history in 1889 at 1,083ft high, and acted as the centerpiece for the centennial of the French Revolution at the 1889 Exposition Universelle World's Fair. This iconic structure has been imitated across the world in Tokyo, Nagoya, New Brighton, Macau, Las Vegas, Hangzhou, Blackpool, and two amusement parks in the United States.

properties.name: Palais de Chaillot
properties.street: 1 Pl. du Trocadéro et du 11 Novembre, 75016 Paris, France
properties.description: The Palais de Chaillot was built for the 1937 Exposition Internationale World's Fair as an architectural compliment to the Eiffel Tower and today is a museum complex featuring: Musée de l'Homme (Anthropology museum), Musée national de la Marine (National Navy Museum), and Cité de l’architecture et du patrimoine (Museum of French Architecture and National Monuments).

properties.name: Musée des Arts Forains
properties.street: 53 Av. des Terroirs de France, 75012 Paris, France
properties.description: The Museum of Fairground Arts is a museum dedicated to historical fairs, including carnivals, world's fairs. The museum itself features French historical fairground games and rides - including a 1920s mirror maze.

properties.name: Musée des transports urbains, interurbains et ruraux
properties.street: 1 Rue Gabriel de Mortillet, 77500 Chelles, France
properties.website: 1 Rue Gabriel de Mortillet, 77500 Chelles, France
properties.description: This is THE French public transportation museum, featuring 4 omnibuses, 13 trams, and 48+ buses from the development of Parisian urban transport.

properties.name: Château de Fontainebleau
properties.description: The Château was THE Summer Palace for French royalty until the construction of Versailles, now the gardens and palace are a museum.

properties.name: Musée du bonbon Haribo
properties.street: Pont des Charrettes, Chem. du Moulin de Bargeton, 30700 Uzès, France
properties.description: Haribo is one of the dominant gummy candy manufacturers in Europe, known for their production of gummy bears - at Uzes you can tour the factory and see how the candy is made.

properties.name: Grotte de Niaux
properties.description: Turns out the French have always been good at painting since there's 13,000+ year old cave art in Niaux Cave. Reservations required - plan ahead.

properties.name: Cité de l'espace
properties.description: This is THE French space museum. However, unlike Cape Canaveral the rockets here are just mockups, but it's the only chance you'll have to go inside of a full sized mockup of the now deorbited MIR space station.
