properties.name: Aeroscopia
properties.description: In the 1970s uncompetitive European aircraft manufacturers merged into Airbus to stand against American competition - Aeroscopia is Airbus's museum. The museum features every single Airbus product every made like the A380, but also has a Concord and Super Guppy.

properties.name: Grotte de Trabuc
properties.street: Route des grottes de Trabuc, 30140 Mialet, France
properties.description: The floor of Trabuc cave is covered in naturally formed miniature spikes as if someone had stood millions of stakes on end.

properties.name: Gouffre de Padirac
properties.description: The Padirac chasm is a 300ft circular hole in the ground leading to an underground river.

properties.name: Grotte des Demoiselles
properties.description: Unlike most caves which are winding, Demoiselles Cave is one giant fairy-tale like room deep in a mountainside.

properties.name: Gouffre de Cabrespine
properties.description: Cabrespine Cave is massive to begin with, and in the middle there is a frighteningly deep circular chasm that stretches past where the eye can see - which is why they built a bridge over it so you can look straight down into the void.

properties.name: Parc Astérix
properties.street: Les Arènes Romaines, Parc Astérix, 60128 Plailly, France
properties.description: Parc Astérix is the largest amusement park in France featuring 10 rollercoasters, including the well renowned Toutatis and OzIris. It's also themed after the popular comic book series Astérix, which I'm sure means more to Europeans than it does to me.

properties.name: Sagrada Família
properties.street: Carrer de Mallorca, 401, Eixample, 08013 Barcelona, Spain
properties.description: This Art Nouveau church was designed in 1882 and has been under construction ever since. Oh and it also looks like a work of alien architecture and is the tallest church in the world.

properties.name: Museo Marítimo de Barcelona
properties.street: Av. de les Drassanes, s/n, Ciutat Vella, 08001 Barcelona, Spain
properties.description: The Kingdom of Spain took all of its money from looting the Americas and spent it on becoming a major naval power. The museum includes a replica of the Galley Real - flagship of the victorious Spanish fleet at the Battle of Lepanto in 1571.

properties.name: Museo del Ferrocarril de Cataluña
properties.street: Plaça d'Eduard Maristany, s/n, 08800 Vilanova i la Geltrú, Barcelona, Spain
properties.description: The Railway Museum of Catalonia has 1854 Mataro, the oldest locomotive in Spain, as well as 30+ other locomotives.

properties.name: PortAventura World
properties.street: Avinguda de l'Alcade Pere Molas, s/n, 43480 Vila-seca, Tarragona, Spain
properties.description: PortAventura World is the largest amusement park in Spain, and has an entire section devoted entirely to Ferrari. Port Aventura has 10 rollercoasters, including: Red Force - the tallest (367ft) and fastest (112mph) rollercoaster in Europe, a rollercoaster themed after barrels of wine, and the official Uncharted (the video game series) rollercoaster.

properties.name: Montaña de sal de Cardona
properties.street: Carr. de la Mina, 6, 08261 Cardona, Barcelona, Spain
properties.description: Salt Mountain is a naturally occurring mountain made entirely out of salt, and so are the ledges of the surrounding valley. Historically, this place has been a salt mine, which is why you can go inside of the artificial salt caverns - which are also filled with salt.

properties.name: Parque natural de Montserrat
properties.street: Abadia de Montserrat Monestir, 08199 Montserrat, Barcelona, Spain
properties.description: Montserrat Mountain looks like a child playing with clay tried their hardest to make a mountain - meaning it's a bunch of lumpy and bulbous cones and funny looking rock formations.

properties.name: Parque nacional de los Picos de Europa
properties.description: Pics de Europa features sheer vertical limestone cliffs such as Naranjo de Bulnes, with hiking trails passing through perilous gorges and abandoned mines. The hiking trail of La Ruta del Cares is carved into the cliffs as it passes through some particularly scenic gorges with natural arches. Mina de Bufferrera features limestone pinnacles and centuries old limestone mines. Like most European national parks, you can't get a good view of anything here unless you get out and hike.

properties.name: Parque de Atracciones Monte Igueldo
properties.street: De Igeldo Ibilbidea, 183, 20008 Donostia / San Sebastián, Gipuzkoa, Spain
properties.description: The top of this mountain is home to an antique amusement park overlooking the ocean, featuring a concrete rollercoaster from 1928 surrounding a lighthouse.

properties.name: Museo Histórico Militar de Asturias
properties.description: During the Great Depression of the 1930s, Spain was caught between worker's revolutionary uprisings, and a coalition of conservative parties that sought to remove democracy. After a coalition of worker's parties defeated the conservatives in the 1936 elections , the military launched a coup to overthrow the government - which failed and plunged the country into the Spanish Civil War. The museum of military history of the Asturias is the most comprehensive museum of the Spanish Civil War. The museum is located in a fortified command post filled with weapons and makeshift armored vehicles constructed during the Civil War.

properties.name: Torre de Hércules
properties.street: Av. Navarra, s/n, 15002 A Coruña, Spain
properties.description: The Lighthouse of Alexandria's plans were used to construct the Tower of Hercules in the first century. This Roman lighthouse is over 2,000+ years old and is where the Romans figuratively believed the world ended since all that lays beyond is the emptiness of the Atlantic.

properties.name: Las Médulas
properties.street: Las Médulas El Bierzo, León, Spain
properties.description: Roman gold mining tore this mountain apart by splitting it at its gold veins using water pressure. What remains is a shattered red landscape carved by water - which makes for really cool hiking.

properties.name: Embalse de Vega de Tera
properties.description: The Vega de Tera dam was built poorly, and collapsed on January 9, 1959 killing 144 people. The remains of the dam are now an area you can hike through, though a smaller dam has been built between the ruins.

properties.name: Muelle de las Carabelas
properties.street: Paraje de La Rábida, s/n, 21819 Palos de la Frontera, Huelva, Spain
properties.description: Christopher Columbus's voyages began the European colonization of the Americas, and Spain built exact replicas of the ships for the 500th anniversary of the voyage.  There's also a museum here dedicated to Columbus's first voyage.

properties.name: Parque Natural de Arribes del Duero
properties.street: 37175 Pereña de la Ribera, Salamanca, Spain
properties.description: Sure the 400 meter deep canyon in Arribes del Duero Natural Park is cool, but the waterfall at Pozo de los Humos is even cooler

properties.name: Delfín (S-61)
properties.street: Av. del Puerto, 03181 Torrevieja, Alicante, Spain
properties.description: The French designed Cold War era Daphné-class submarine Delfín is the only Spanish submarine you can go inside of.

properties.name: Barrancos de Gebas
properties.description: Spain turned the Badlands of Barrancos de Gebas into a reservoir, which means that this piece of geography ordinarily known for being dry is instead awash in sharp blue water.

properties.name: Museo Histórico Militar de Cartagena
properties.street: Pl. Puerta de la Serreta, s/n, 30201 Cartagena, Murcia, Spain
properties.description: This is THE Spanish artillery museum. The Military History Museum of Cartagena has 40+ artillery pieces and a few tanks.

properties.name: Museo Naval de Cartagena
properties.street: P.º Alfonso XII, s/n, 30201 Cartagena, Murcia, Spain
properties.description: The Naval Museum of Cartagena has the 1889 submarine Peral - the first military capable submarine ever built.

properties.name: Parque nacional de Ordesa y Monte Perdido
properties.description: Ordesa y Monte Perdido National Park covers distinct waterfall filled canyons within the Pyrenees mountains such as the Gargantas de Escuaín,Cañón de Añisclo, and Cañón del Vellos . There's a lot of hiking to do, but the roads A-138, and A-135 let you get some pretty good views. Unfortunately the best views of the narrow gorges requires hiking.

properties.name: Desierto de Tabernas
properties.description: The Tabernas Desert is the only actual desert in Europe - and it looks so much like the American Southwest that it's littered in Hollywood movie sets so studios could avoid paying American wages.

properties.name: Alhambra
properties.street: C. Real de la Alhambra, s/n, Centro, 18009 Granada, Spain
properties.description: Part of the Iberian peninsula was once ruled by the Muslim state of the Emirate of Grenada - which built a decadent palace on a hilltop fortress in Grenada in 1238AD. Following the Reconquista, the Alhambra became the Royal Court for Spain - and a European palace was later built atop the Islamic architecture.

properties.name: El Torcal de Antequera
properties.street: Paraje Natural Torcal de Antequera, Ctra. de Acceso Al Torcal Alto Km 3,5, Antequera, Málaga, Spain
properties.description: The tops of the cliffs of the El Torcal Massif de are a rugged Karst landscape where towers of rocks have formed a jumbled maze of narrow canyons and spires. There's well established hiking trails to get the best views, however the road to the visitor center captures the unique landscape fairly well.

properties.name: Tajo de Ronda
properties.description: La Ronda is split in two by a 100 meter deep gorge, which remarkably has a masonry bridge spanning it from 1794

properties.name: Bardenas Reales
properties.description: Northern Spain is covered in the semi-arid badlands of the Bardenas Reales, which features colorful eroded landscape and tumbleweeds like you would see at Badlands National Park in the United States.

properties.name: Parque natural del Cañón del Río Lobos
properties.street: Casa del Parque Cañón de Río lobos, Carretera SO-920, Km. 16, 42317 El Burgo de Osma, Soria, Spain
properties.description: The ordinary Rio Lobos Canyon turns into colorful carved karst cliffs at its heart near the Hermitage of San Bartolomé

properties.name: Monasterio de Piedra
properties.street: Monasterio de Piedra C. Afueras, s/n, 50210 Nuévalos, Zaragoza, Spain
properties.description: The ruins of the Stone Monastery are surrounded by cliffs, caves, lakes, and waterfalls that look like a lush green oasis in the surrounding orange landscape.

properties.name: Ciudad Encantada
properties.street: Carretera CM-2104, Km 19, 16146 Valdecabras, Cuenca, Spain
properties.description: The limestone rocks of the Enchanted City have been carved down to dolomite, leaving a maze of mushroom shaped rocks, arches, and overhangs.

properties.name: Parque natural del Alto Tajo
properties.street: Ermita de la Virgen de la Hoz 19392 Corduente, Guadalajara, Spain
properties.description: The Tagus river carved the red and gray limestone of Alto Tajo Natural Park into the twisted gorges and stacks of Barranco de la Hoz and Hundido de Armallones. The hiking trails have bridges hammered into the sides of the cliffs so you'll be near the river through any hike you choose.

properties.name: Museo del Ferrocarril de Madrid
properties.street: Paseo de las Delicias, 61, Arganzuela, 28045 Madrid, Spain
properties.description: This is THE Spanish railway museum. Located in a former 1880s train station the Railway Museum of Madrid features 25+ locomotives, including: the streamlined and futuristic Talgo II, and some of the first locomotives to ever operate in Spain.

properties.name: Templo de Debod
properties.street: C. de Ferraz, 1, Moncloa - Aravaca, 28008 Madrid, Spain
properties.description: Why travel to Egypt to see an ancient Egyptian temple when instead you can go to Madrid where they've conveniently relocated one for you. The 200 BC Temple of Debod would have been flooded by the Aswan High Dam, but was instead moved to Spain in 1968.

properties.name: Museo de Aeronáutica y Astronáutica
properties.street: Autovía del Suroeste, km 10, Latina, 28024 Madrid, Spain
properties.description: This is THE Spanish aviation museum, featuring 114+ aircraft. Historically, most of Spain's aviation has been licensed construction and NATO handouts. However, the autogyro was invented in Spain meaning there are a notable number of helicopters at the Air and Space Museum.

properties.name: Valle de los Caídos
properties.street: Carretera de Guadarrama/El Escorial, 28209 San Lorenzo de El Escorial, Madrid, Spain
properties.description: Most National Cemeteries are in pointy shaped buildings or spread across fields of graves - Spain's is on top of a mountain with the largest cross in the world.

properties.name: Parque Warner Madrid
properties.street: A-4, salida 22, 28330 San Martín de la Vega, Madrid, Spain
properties.description: Warner Bros. has their own amusement parks just like Universal Studios, but with only 7 rollercoasters.

properties.name: Museo de Falúas Reales
properties.street: Jardín Del Príncipe, s/n, 28300 Aranjuez, Madrid, Spain
properties.description: The Royal Barge Museum is full of 6 of the most elaborate rowing boats you'll ever see - because a King has to be moved in style.

properties.name: Museo del Prado
properties.street: Museo Nacional del Prado, Retiro, 28014 Madrid, Spain
properties.description: Spain got really rich from looting the Americas, and used the money to purchase lots of paintings and sculptures - including a understudy of Leonardo Da Vinci's contemporary version of the Mona Lisa.

properties.name: Gil Eannes (navio-hospital)
properties.street: Navio Gil Eannes - Doca Comercial, 4900-321 Viana do Castelo, Portugal
properties.description: The 1955 Hospital Ship Gilles Eannes later became a tug, icebreaker, mailboat, supply ship, passenger liner, and refrigerated cargo ship - which means that touring it is a chaotic whirlwind of maritime history.

properties.name: Museu Nacional Ferroviário
properties.street: Rua Engenheiro, R. Ferreira de Mesquita 1 A, 2330-152 Entroncamento, Portugal
properties.description: Portuguese railroading is an offshoot of British locomotives design - as most of the original locomotives at the National Railway Museum are British built. The National Railway Museum includes the 1862 Portuguese Royal Train, the Portuguese Presidential Train used by dictator Antonio Salazar, and 17+ other locomotives.

properties.name: Praça-forte de Peniche
properties.description: The 1558 Peniche Fortress acted as the political prison of the Estado Novo regime (1933-1974) during Portugal's dictatorship under Antonio Salazar. The prison is now home to the National Museum of Resistance and Liberty dedicated to preserving the memory of the fight against the dictatorship that culminated in the success of the Carnation Revolution and return to democracy in 1974.

properties.name: Minas de Aljustel
properties.description: The Aljustrel lead and zinc mine is filled with exciting colors and possible lead poisoning - but the tunnels are electric blue!

properties.name: Dom Fernando II e Glória (UAM203)
properties.street: LG Alfredo Dinis, Cacilhas, 2800-252 Almada, Portugal
properties.description: The 1845 sailing frigate Dom Fernando II e Glória is the oldest Portuguese ship still afloat - and one of the few purely sailing frigates left in the world. The frigate is  also available for tour, along with the Cold War era Albacore-class submarine NRP Barracuda.

properties.name: Museu Nacional dos Coches
properties.description: When you're the royalty of Portugal, you can afford to have the most expensive and ornate carriages imaginable - and 45+ were collected at the National Coach Museum in Lisbon.

properties.name: Museu de Marinha
properties.street: Praça do Império, Santa Maria de Belém, 1400-206 Lisboa, Portugal
properties.description: The barge pavilion of the Portuguese National Maritime Museum has 6+ elaborate royal barges that the Royalty of Portugal used to move around the Tagus River in Lisbon. There's also the first seaplane to cross the South Atlantic.

properties.name: Museu do Ar
properties.street: Granja do Marquês, 2715-021 Pêro Pinheiro, Portugal
properties.description: The Portuguese Air Museum isn't the largest air museum as there's only 48+ aircraft, but it does have a replica of Santos Dumont's 14-bis - one of the first European aircraft to fly.

properties.name: Palácio Nacional da Pena
properties.description: Most European palaces are painted some shade of opulent white - the 1854 Pena National Palace is bright red, yellow, and purple.

properties.name: Quinta da Regaleira
properties.description: A bunch of Rich Portuguese people built this mansion over time, and built an extensive system of gardens, caves, tunnels, inverted towers, and waterfalls.

properties.name: Marinemuseet
properties.street: Karljohansvern, Kommandørkaptein Klincks vei 9, 3183 Horten, Norway
properties.description: Norway has historically been a naval power - Vikings got around by using boats after all. The Norwegian Naval Museum tracks the history of the Norwegian Navy, and is notably home to the Cold War era Kobben-class submarine KNM Utstein, the Cold War era Oslo-class frigate KNM Narvik, the Storm-class patrol boat KBM Blink, and Norway's first torpedo boat from 1873.

properties.name: Oscarsborg festning
properties.description: This is one of the few naval fortresses still in existence that can claim to have sunk an enemy vessel. The 1855 Oscarsborg Fortress guards the entrance to Oslo by sea, and notoriously sunk a Nazi heavy cruiser during WW2 using the fortress's outdated equipment - significantly delaying the Nazi invasion of Norway.

properties.name: Frammuseet
properties.description: This is THE arctic exploration museum. The Fram was custom built as an arctic exploration ship in 1893, and survived 3 years in the ice during Nansen's Fram Expedition, mapped the arctic islands near western Greenland, and successfully carried out the first expedition to reach the South Pole. The museum also has the Gjøa - the first ship to compete the Northwest Passage. Both ships are displayed fully intact - and are available for tour.

properties.name: Kon-Tiki Museet
properties.description: Thor Heyerdahl proved that ancient trans-pacific travel was possible when he sailed the primitive raft Kon-Tiki from South America to the Tuamotu Islands in 1947. He also showed that ancient transatlantic travel was possible with primitive reed boats when he sailed the Ra II from Africa to Barbados. Both ships are on display at the Kon-Tiki museum along with some of the artifacts Heyerdahl collected in his travels.

properties.name: Vikingskipshuset
properties.description: The shallow-draft longships used to navigate the Fjords of Norway turned out to be very well suited for Vikings pillaging all of Europe. The 9th century Gokstad longship was buried underground - meaning that it's nearly perfectly intact. Learn all about the Vikings and see other artifacts at the Viking Ship Museum.

properties.name: Sporveismuseet Vognhall 5
properties.description: Because Europeans are allergic to cars, they have a lot of nice public transit museums - and the Oslo Transport Museum has 25+ trams and 10+ buses on display at Depot 5.

properties.name: Forsvarets Flysamling Gardermoen
properties.description: Unlike it's neighbor Sweden, Norway does not produce its own aircraft - meaning their airforce is composed of aircraft from other countries that could be bought. Notable aircraft include the Rumpler Taube which was the first aircraft ever flown in Norway in 1912, and a C-130.

properties.name: Norsk jernbanemuseum
properties.description: The Norwegian Railway Museum includes the Norwegian Royal Train and the largest steam locomotive ever operated in Norway. There's only 10+ trains here - but the museum offers a better curated experience than most, as narrow gauge and miniature trains operate during the summer.

properties.name: Norsk vegmuseum
properties.description: The deceptively named Norwegian Road Museum is actually the museum complex of: The Norwegian Road Museum, the 100+ vehicles of the Norwegian Vehicle History Museum, and the tunnels and mining equipment of the Norwegian Mountain Exploration Museum.

properties.name: Blaafarveværket
properties.description: Blue dye used to be made out of the toxic heavy metal Cobalt - and now you can explore the waterfalls and 1850s Cobalt mining tunnels at this open-air industrial site.

properties.name: Norsk luftfartsmuseum
properties.description: The Norwegian Aviation Museum is Norway's primary aviation museum - and houses 40+ aircraft - which isn't a lot. However, they do have a crashed Junkers Ju 88 which is displayed as it was when it crashed, and a U2 spyplane which was stationed in Bodo to spy on the USSR.

properties.name: Lofotr Vikingmuseum
properties.description: This place has a replica Viking longhouse and Viking longship. The longhouse is based on the largest Viking structure ever found - which was discovered nearby in 1983.

properties.name: Hurtigrutemuseet
properties.description: Before the construction of roads in the 1940s, Northern Norway communities were only accessible by sea. The Coastal Express passenger ship service was chartered by Norway to make connection possible. The Coastal Express Museum houses the 1956 coastal express ship MS Finnmarken enclosed in a glass building.

properties.name: Reisa nasjonalpark
properties.description: Despite being so far north, the Reisa river valley is lush and full of waterfalls and reindeer - the only problem is that accessing requires hiking through the wilderness from a remote road.

properties.name: Frafjordheiene
properties.description: The Frafjordheiene Landscape Protection Area has tall vertical fjords with waterfalls - and lakes on top of the mountains themselves. The park is well known for Kjerag (the mountain with a boulder wedged between its cliffs), Eikeskofossen waterfall, Kalleliklimpen waterfall, and Fossjuvet waterfall and gorge. The hiking trails are fairly well defined, but it's a mountain - so it's not an easy hike.

properties.name: Folgefonna nasjonalpark
properties.description: Hike up to glacial lakes on top of mountains to see the remnants of glaciers that once covered most of Europe during the ice age. It's a mountain of ice on top of a mountain with waterfalls streaming down the valleys.

properties.name: Trolltunga
properties.description: Troll Tongue rock juts off of a 2300ft tall cliff above a lake among snow covered mountaintops. It's a 17 miles hike that takes 10 hours minimum - and it is busy.

properties.name: Vøringsfossen
properties.description: Two 500ft+ waterfalls converge in a gorge spanned by a pedestrian bridge offering the best views.

properties.name: Sagastad
properties.description: Sagastad has a replica of the Myklebust Ship, the largest Viking ship ever found -and you can walk on the deck of it. The rest of the museum isn't that interesting.

properties.name: Jostedalsbreen nasjonalpark
properties.street: Jostedalsbreen National Park Center Sandvik, 6799 Oppstryn, Norway
properties.description: Jostedalsbreen is the largest glacier in Europe - the ice cap stretches from 300-2000meters and the river valleys created my the streams are full of waterfalls and rushing water. This isn't America, you have to hike a few miles to get anywhere close to the park.

properties.name: Suomen ilmavoimamuseo
properties.description: The Finnish Air Force remained a persistent menace to the Soviet Union during the Winter War and Continuation War, and the Finnish Air Force Museum is mainly dedicated to the ragtag set of aircraft Finland used to defend itself from Communist oppression. There's also the aircraft that the Soviet Union used to try to oppress the Finnish during the Cold War for a total of 40+ aircraft.

properties.name: Suomen merimuseo
properties.description: The Finnish Maritime Museum is home to the 1907 icebreaker Tarmo (seized by the Finnish from the Soviets during the Finnish Civil War), and the 1900 lightship Kemi. There's also a few examples of Finnish watercraft and a patrol boat in the main hall.

properties.name: Forum Marinum
properties.description: This is THE Finnish maritime museum. Featuring 13+ ships including the 1960 cruise ship MS Bore, Cold War era minelayer Keihässalmi, Cold War era Turunmaa-class gunboat Karjala, the 1887 barque Sigyn, sailing cargo ship Suomen Joutsen, and 6 other ships such as torpedo boats and tugboats.

properties.name: Tytyrin kaivos
properties.description: The Tytyrin calcium mine has been operating for so long that the calcium has begun dripping everywhere, forming haunting stalactites that you can see as you tour through the tunnels.

properties.name: Linnanmäki
properties.description: Linnanmäki is the oldest and largest amusement park in Finland - featuring 8 rollercoasters including one of the last remaining side-friction rollercoasters in the world.

properties.name: Suomen Rautatiemuseo
properties.description: Finnish railroading started off as an extension of the Russian Empire's railway system- later supplemented by American, English, Austrian, Swiss, and German locomotives. As a result the Finnish Railway Museum has an eclectic mix of 25+ European and American locomotives.

properties.name: Panssarimuseo
properties.description: The Parola Tank Museum has an armored train and 40+ tanks. Featuring one of the most extensive collection of Soviet armored vehicles outside of Russia.

properties.name: Museo Militaria
properties.description: Finland combined the Artillery Museum of Finland with the Military Engineer, and Military Signals Museum to create the Military Museum of Finland. Featuring 90+ guns with a strong collection of Russian Empire and Soviet Union equipment.

properties.name: Sotamuseon Maneesi
properties.description: The Manage Military Museum features the Finnish interwar submarine Vesikko on the fortress island of Suomenlinna guarding Helsinki's harbor.

properties.name: Vanatknika Varjupaik
properties.street: Lai tn 1, Järva-Jaani, 73301 Järva maakond, Estonia
properties.description: This is THE Estonian vehicle museum. It's called OldTech Park because it's 500+ Soviet vehicles rusting in a field - buses, trams, trucks, cars, tanks, tractors, cranes, firetrucks, newspaper stands, tollbooths, and harvesters - this place has everything in authentic dilapidated Soviet condition.

properties.name: Eesti Kaevandusmuuseum
properties.street: Jaama tn 100, Kohtla-Nõmme, 30503 Ida-Viru maakond, Estonia
properties.description: The Estonian Mining museum is an abandoned Soviet shale quarry where you can now roam through the rust covered tunnels and hope that it's still safe.

properties.name: Eesti Põllumajandusmuuseum
properties.description: OldTech Park doesn't have a lot of tractors, but the Estonian Agricultural Museum does - with 25+ ancient tractors and informative history about farming in Estonia.

properties.name: Eesti Meremuuseum
properties.description: This is THE Baltic maritime museum. The Estonian Maritime Museum is located in a 1930s concrete seaplane hangar and features 17 ships, including: the Estonian WW2 era Kalev-class minelaying submarine EML Lembit, the Russian Empire's 1912 icebreaker Suur Tõll, 4 patrol boats, and an assortment of fishing trawlers and coast guard vessels.

properties.name: Eesti Sõjamuuseum - Kindral Laidoneri Muuseum
properties.street: Mõisa tee 1, Viimsi, 74001 Harju maakond, Estonia
properties.description: Estonia is located between the major powers of Europe, and therefore was conquered by the Teutonic Order, Denmark, Poland, Sweden, and the Russian Empire. After briefly gaining independence from 1918-1940, Estonia was conquered by the Soviet Union, conquered by the Nazis in 1941, conquered AGAIN by the Soviet Union in 1945 before ultimately gaining independence (again) in 1991. The Estonian War Museum features an armored train, 24 artillery pieces, and a variety of tanks and armored vehicles from Estonia's long history of war.

properties.name: Rīgas Motormuzejs
properties.street: Bruno, Sergeja Eizenšteina iela 8, Vidzemes priekšpilsēta, Rīga, LV-1079, Latvia
properties.description: The Riga Motormuseum is focused on the telling the story of the development of the European automotive industry - including the Soviet Union's attempts at making a reliable car.

properties.name: Latvijas dzelzceļa vēstures muzejs
properties.street: Uzvaras bulvāris 2A, Zemgales priekšpilsēta, Rīga, LV-1048, Latvia
properties.description: The Latvian Railway Museum has 15+ trains from when the Soviet Union conquered the country - unlike most Soviet Trains in museums, these ones are in good condition and you can go inside of them.

properties.name: Rīgas Aviācijas muzejs
properties.street: Skultes iela 35, Skulte, Mārupes pagasts, Mārupes novads, LV-2108, Latvia
properties.description: Like most aviation museums in Eastern Europe, the Riga Aviation Museum is a bunch (37+) of Eastern Bloc planes rusting in a field. Including the MiG-23, MiG-25, MiG-27, MiG-29, Sukhoi Su-7,  Yak-28, Tu-22, and large transport helicopter Mil Mi-6.

properties.name: Līgatnes Padomju slepenais bunkurs
properties.street: Skaļupes, Līgatne, Cēsu nov, LV-4108, Latvia
properties.description: The people of the Latvian SSR could sleep soundly knowing that their leaders had generously insulated themselves from the threat of nuclear war by constructing a secret bunker from which they would continue to rule over them. Tour the continuation-of-government facility for Latvia's communist government and see how communism planned to outlive capitalism at the end of the world.

properties.name: Liepājas Karostas cietums
properties.description: At the Karosta Prison Museum the museum guards will  abuse you in historically accurate to communism ways by putting you in a prison uniform, locking you in a cell, and interrogating you.

properties.name: Plokštinės raketų bazė
properties.street: Šilinės gatvė 4, Plokščių k, 90419 Plungės r. sav., Lithuania
properties.description: Cold War Museum is a gentle name for "This is a Soviet Nuclear Missile Base". The museum is located inside Žemaitijos National Park and also includes tours of an abandoned Soviet military town. You need to reserve a ticket ahead of time.

properties.name: Lietuvos jūrų muziejus
properties.street: Smiltynės g. 3, Klaipėda, 93100 Klaipėdos m. sav., Lithuania
properties.description: The Lithuanian Sea Museum is an aquarium located inside of the Prussian Kopgalio Fortress. The museum includes the aquarium, fortress, and an assortment of fishing vessels.

properties.name: Grūto parkas
properties.description: Lithuanians love sculpture parks, and during decommunization moved all of the torn-down Soviet monuments into a single park - which also features a museum of Soviet propaganda, and a zoo.

properties.name: Kauno tvirtovės IX fortas
properties.street: Žemaičių pl. 73, Kaunas, 47435 Kauno m. sav., Lithuania
properties.description: Russia built this fortress to guard Lithuania from German aggression in 1914. After independence, the Lithuanians used it as a prison. The fortress was then used by the invading Soviets to kill political prisoners during the Soviet invasion in 1940, and then used by the Nazis to kill 50,000+ people during the Holocaust. The fortress was then again used by a prison by the Soviet Union . The fortress is now a memorial to the victims killed at the IX Fortress.

properties.name: Siauruko muziejus
properties.street: Stoties g. 4 A, Anykščiai, 29107 Anykščių r. sav., Lithuania
properties.description: It's Soviet Trains - but tiny. The Narrow Gauge Railroad Museum contains a collection of Soviet narrow gauge locomotives, as well as a section devoted to Eastern Bloc automobiles.

properties.name: Automuziejus Vilnius
properties.street: Dariaus ir Girėno g. 2, Vilnius, 02158 Vilniaus m. sav., Lithuania
properties.description: The Vilnius Automobile Museum is has 100+ vehicles, including several Lithuanian Presidential vehicles.

properties.name: Lietuvos nacionalinis muziejus
properties.street: Arsenalo g. 1, Vilnius, 01143 Vilniaus m. sav., Lithuania
properties.description: The Lithuanian National Museum is located on the grounds of the former Vilnius Castle Complex, and includes the recently rebuilt Palace of the Grand Dukes of Lithuania. The museum covers Lithuanian history - which involved being conquered by the Teutonic Knights, forming an independent Grand Duchy of Lithuania, joining with Poland to form the powerful Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, being conquered by Russia, successfully fighting for independence, then being conquered by the Soviet Union.

properties.name: Okupacijų ir laisvės kovų muziejus
properties.street: Aukų g. 2A, Vilnius, 01400 Vilniaus m. sav., Lithuania
properties.description: The Museum of Occupation and Freedom March is located in the former KGB headquarters in Lithuania - where the communist secret police maintained their iron grip over the freedom of Lithuanians. The building features a reconstruction of the KGB prison that was once there, and extensive history on the forced deportations carried out by the Soviet Union in an attempt to destroy the Lithuanian people.

properties.name: Yomiuriland
properties.description: Yomiuriland isn't the biggest or best amusement park in Japan - but it does have PokéPark Kanto - which is basically Pokémon but in real life. The rollercoaster Bandit was the fastest rollercoaster in the world when it opened here in 1988.

properties.name: Kołobrzeski Skansen Morski
properties.description: The Kołobrzeg Maritime Open-Air Museum has the Soviet Cold War era project 012 (NATO: Obluze) patrol ship ORP Fala and the Cold War era project 205 (NATO: Osa) missile boat ORP Władysławowo. The ships are in fairly rough shape - but so is everything the Soviet Union touched.

properties.name: Muzeum Oręża Polskiego w Kołobrzegu
properties.description: The Polish Arms Museum in Kołobrzeg features a collection of polish weapons and armor from the Middle Ages to present. The museum is located in a 15th century Hanseatic Merchant's tenement house, and features a large selection of Soviet armored vehicles and missile launchers in its outdoor pavilion.

properties.name: Muzeum Zimnej Wojny w Podborsku
properties.street: Muzeum Zimnej Wojny w Podborsku 78-220 Podborsko, Poland
properties.description: Explore a Soviet Nuclear Bomb storage facility designed to withstand nuclear strikes at the Podborsko Cold War Museum. The Soviets set up this facility in 1967, and used it until they withdrew from Poland in 1992.

properties.name: Wilczy Szaniec
properties.description: Nazi officers tried and failed to assassinate Adolf Hitler at the Wolf's Lair command center on July 20, 1944. Now the decaying and overgrown concrete bunker is a tourist site.

properties.name: Zamek w Malborku
properties.description: Malbork Castle is the largest castle in the world by area. German crusaders called the Teutonic Order ruled over northern Poland from 1230-1466, and built this castle as part of their crusades against the Pagans in Eastern Europe. The castle later became the arsenal of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, and residence of the Polish King .

properties.name: KZ Stutthof
properties.description: When the Nazis invaded Poland during WW2 they rounded up Polish leadership and intellectuals for their extermination at Stutthof concentration camp. Ultimately 65,000 people were killed at Stutthof. Learn about the horror humanity will inflict on others at the museum here.

properties.name: Muzeum Kolejnictwa w Kościerzynie
properties.description: The Railway Museum in Kościerzyna has 25+ locomotives from Polish railroading history. They're mostly rusting away, but that's par for the course for Eastern European railroading museums.

properties.name: Muzeum Techniki Wojskowej Gryf
properties.description: The Gryf Museum of Military technology collects tanks and antique cars - and makes them functional so they can hold mock battles. There are 100+ vehicles here, as well as a 'sapper' museum, and command bunker.

properties.name: ORP Błyskawica
properties.street: al. Jana Pawła II 1, 81-345 Gdynia, Poland
properties.description: This is the oldest destroyer still in existence. Before WW2, Poland built fast and heavily armed destroyers for operations in the Baltic. The ORP Błyskawica escaped to the United Kingdom before the Nazis invaded, then took part in the Norwegian Campaign, the Dunkirk Evacuation, and convoy escorting during WW2. The ship has been lovingly preserved and is available for tour.

properties.name: Muzeum Marynarki Wojennej w Gdyni
properties.description: This is THE Polish Navy museum. After WW1 the Poland was granted sea access via the independent nation of the Free City of Danzig - which remained full of German nationalists. The Polish government instead decided to build a new major seaport in the then tiny city of Gydnia - and turned it into the headquarters of the Polish Navy. The Gdynia Naval Museum is the home to the interwar-era destroyer ORP Błyskawica (docked 0.5km away), the Cold War era Type 207 submarine ORP Sokół, and the interwar-era patrol cutter ORP Batory.

properties.name: Muzeum Westerplatte
properties.street: Centrum Obsługi Zwiedzjacych, mjr. Henryka Sucharskiego 77, 80-601 Gdańsk, Poland
properties.description: During the Nazi invasion of Poland, 240 Polish soldiers defended the Westerplatte peninsula for 7 days against 3,400 Nazis. The ruins of the battlefield still stand today, and have been turned into the Westerplatte Museum.

properties.name: Muzeum II Wojny Światowej w Gdańsku
properties.description: During WW2 Poland was invaded by the Nazis and Soviets in 1939, who both proceeded to massacre Polish leadership and genocide the Polish people. Poland's total death toll from WW2 was 6,028,000 killed, more than 16% of its pre-war population. The end of the war replaced the Nazi occupiers with total Soviet domination of Poland - which would not end until 1989. The WW2 Museum in Gdansk follows Polish history in WW2.

properties.name: Narodowe Muzeum Morskie w Gdańsku
properties.description: The National Maritime Museum of Gdańsk features the first ship built in Poland after WW2 - the SS Soldek - which is a surviving Eastern bloc ship from 1949. The museum building focuses on the history of polish sailing, and is located next to a medieval harbor crane from 1444.

properties.name: Muzeum Komunikacji w Paterku
properties.description: This is THE Polish bus museum - and by that I mean it's 30+ (mostly Communist) buses rotting in a field.

properties.name: Park Cytadela
properties.description: Citadel Park is built on top of the overgrown ruins of the 1830 Prussian Fort Winiary. The tunnels of the fortress are also home to the armored vehicles and guns of the Museum of Armaments, and the Poznań Army Museum.

properties.name: Muzeum Martyrologii Wielkopolan – Fort VII w Poznaniu
properties.description: The Prussians built Fort VII in 1880 as part of a ring of fortifications around Poznań. After the Nazis invaded Poland they used it as a concentration camp to kill 20,000 poles. The overgrown ruins of the fort are now a somber memorial to those that died.

properties.name: Muzeum Broni Pancernej w Poznaniu
properties.description: The Armored Weapons Museum features 23+ tanks - including interwar Polish tankettes. There's also a large assortment of artillery, trucks, and support vehicles - all of which are in good condition (instead of rusting in a field).

properties.name: Muzeum Narodowe Rolnictwa i Przemysłu Rolno-Spożywczego w Szreniawie
properties.description: This is THE Polish farming museum. The Szreniawa National Museum of Agriculture and Agri-Food Industry consists of an entire farm - and everything that goes into supporting a farm. That means there's cropdusters, trains, buildings full of farm vehicles and 21+ carriages, and steam powered tractors

properties.name: Muzeum Obozów Jenieckich w Żaganiu
properties.description: The Museum of POW Camps in Żagań commemorates Stalag Luft III - a prisoner-of-war camp for Western Allied air force personnel. Stalag Luft III was the site of The Great Escape - where Allied airmen tunneled their way out of the camp, though many were killed by the Nazis when they were later caught.

properties.name: Lubuskie Muzeum Wojskowe
properties.description: The Lubuskie Military Museum isn't the largest military museum in Poland, but it does have 23 artillery pieces - a larger number than most museums. There's also 24 tracked vehicles, 25 aircraft, and a few dozen trucks. Most of the collection is Eastern Bloc equipment.

properties.name: Muzeum Techniki Rolniczej i Gospodarstwa Wiejskiego w Redczu Krukowym
properties.description: This is the other major agricultural museum in Poland. The Redecz Krukowy Museum of Agricultural Technology and Rural Economy is the private collection of Janusz Borkowski - who filled 10 sheds with his horde of agricultural equipment, carriages, trains, cars, and military vehicles.

properties.name: Muzeum Polskiej Techniki Wojskowej
properties.description: This is THE polish military museum, featuring 36+ armored vehicles, 22+ aircraft, 30+ artillery pieces, countless trucks, and a Soyuz space capsule - all rusting in a field surrounding Fort IX of the 19th century Russian Warsaw Fortress.

properties.name: Łazienki Królewskie w Warszawie
properties.description: Royals Baths Park was the summer palace for Polish Royalty, who turned it into a park-and-palace complex with the Palace on the Isle as its centerpiece. The park is full of palaces-turned-art-museums including: Ujazdów Castle, The Belweder, Myślewicki Palace, and The White House.

properties.name: Pałac Kultury i Nauki
properties.description: The Soviets built an 778ft art-deco skyscraper in the middle of Warsaw - which came to become a symbol of Soviet domination over Poland. The building now features a museum complex, including: the cold war stylings of the Neon Museum, The National Museum of Technology in Warsaw, and the Museum of Evolution.

properties.name: Stacja Muzeum
properties.description: This is THE Polish train museum. The Station Museum in Warsaw has 34 locomotives, with most of them being pre-WW2 Polish and German steam locomotives. Notably, the streamlined pm3 is here.

properties.name: Muzeum Powstania Warszawskiego
properties.description: During WW2 Poland was occupied by the Nazis, and Polish cities were converted into walled prisons as part of their ongoing genocide against the Polish people. As the end of the war loomed in 1944, the Polish launched a nationwide uprising to try to reclaim the country before the Soviet occupiers returned. The Soviets stood by and offered no help as the uprising was crushed, 200,000 Polish citizens were killed in mass executions, and Warsaw was punitively systemically demolished in an attempt to erase Polish cultural heritage. The Warsaw Uprising Museum tells the story of Poland's final push for freedom before Soviet domination erased democracy.

properties.name: Cytadela Warszawska
properties.description: The Russian Empire built the Warsaw Citadel to solidify control over the freedom-seeking Polish. The fortress is now a museum complex featuring: the guns and armor of the Polish Army Museum, the tales of the repeated invasions of Poland by Germany and Russia at the Polish History Museum, the Katyn Museum, and Museum of the 10th Pavilion of the Warsaw Citadel.

properties.name: Muzeum im. Orła Białego
properties.description: The White Eagle Museum is home to artillery and armored vehicles rusting in a field - some of which are used to give visitors rides, there's also the Cold War era Project 664 torpedo boat ORP Odważny, and the ruins of the Rejow steel works.

properties.name: KL Majdanek
properties.description: The Nazis built Majdanek as a concentration camp for forced labor, but later converted it into an extermination camp as part of the plan for genocide of the Polish people and Polish Jews. The Nazis tore down most of their extermination camps before they were captured in an attempt to hide their atrocities, but the Soviets captured Majdanek before that could happen. 78,000 people were killed at Majdanek by the Nazis. The Soviets later used Majdanek to imprison Polish freedom fighters. The site is now a museum, and the extermination camp and its gas chambers are largely intact.

properties.name: Muzeum Sił Powietrznych w Dęblinie
properties.description: The Dęblin Air Force Museum is a museum of the Polish Air Force featuring 80+ mostly Eastern Bloc aircraft. Notable features include a Mil Mi-6 heavy lift helicopter, a Yak-40 luxury passenger plane, and various portable radar dishes.

properties.name: Krzyżtopór
properties.description: In 1644 a Polish Nobleman built an expensive Italian styled palace in the heart of Poland - so expensive that it cost too much to fix after it was ransacked by the Swedish in 1655. Now you can wander around the ruins.

properties.name: Muzeum Polskiej Motoryzacji XX wieku w Busku-Zdroju
properties.description: The 20th Century Polish Automotive Museum is dedicated to collecting ONLY Polish vehicles - and has 120+ of them. The museum is still starting out - so you need to reserve a date to visit or they will not let you in.

properties.name: Muzeum Drogownictwa w Szczucinie
properties.description: The Szczucin Road Museum is a museum of road building, and features 30+ antique construction vehicles that demonstrate the evolution of Polish road construction.

properties.name: Kopalnia ropy naftowej w Bóbrce
properties.description: Oil and gas spontaneously surfaces in the Bóbrka area of Poland, and dedicated mining began in 1854 - extraction has continued to this day. The Ignacy Łukasiewicz Museum of the Oil and Gas Industry features 3 modern oil wells and their support equipment, as well as the historical Franek and Janina wells.

properties.name: Kopalnia soli Wieliczka
properties.description: Polish miners have been extracting salt from the Wieliczka Salt Mine since the 13 century, and have carved the cavernous spaces into intricate sculptures - including an entire chapel.

properties.name: Kopalnia Soli Bochnia
properties.description: The Bochnia Salt Mine has been operating since 1248, and the Polish miners have carved the mine into churches and sculptures. However, it's not as fancy as the nearby Wieliczka Salt Mine. This mine however sets itself apart as there are underground ferry rides through the caverns.

properties.name: Muzeum Lotnictwa Polskiego
properties.street: al. Jana Pawła II 39, 31-864 Kraków, Poland
properties.description: This is THE Polish aircraft museum. The Polish Aviation Museum features 200+ aircraft, including the only surviving Polish-built military aircraft from WW2. The rest of the aircraft here include almost all aircraft used in Poland after WW2 - and in fine Eastern European tradition they are rusting in a field.

properties.name: Zamek Królewski na Wawelu
properties.description: Wawel Castle in Kraków was the seat of power of the Polish monarchy when the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth was the strongest land-power in Europe, which means the insides are really nice. The castle is now an art museum with a massive collection of lavish tents captured from the Ottoman Empire.

properties.name: Ojcowski Park Narodowy
properties.description: Ojców National Park is a valley full of white limestone columns surrounded by green forest. The hiking trails let you follow the rim of the valley and walk right next to some of the best formations. The Maczuga Herkulesa is a standalone stack that is 30 meters high.

properties.name: Energylandia
properties.description: Energylandia is best amusement park in Poland, and one of the largest amusement parks in the world. Featuring 19 rollercoasters, including the critically acclaimed Zadra and Hyperion.

properties.name: KZ Auschwitz
properties.description: Auschwitz Concentration Camp was the largest single facility dedicated to genocide ever constructed. 1.1 million people were killed here, and the facility is so large that the camps surround the town of Oświęcim. Auschwitz I has the infamous 'Aerbeit mach frei' entryway, while Auschwitz II-Birkenau has the gatehouse. This is not a happy place.

properties.name: Muzeum Powstań Śląskich
properties.description: Following the defeat of the German Empire in WW1, the valuable industrialized lands of Silesia was slated for a vote on whether to join Germany or Poland - the only problem was that Silesia was filled with a near equal amount of Polish and Germans. German forces tried to maintain control by force, and the Polish rose against them, ethnic paramilitary groups also fought one another - leading to escalating mutual atrocities. The uprisings lead to Polish control over roughly half of Silesia. The Silesian Uprising Museum tells the story of the uprisings, and features two replica improvised armored cars.

properties.name: Kopaliny (kopalnia uranu)
properties.description: Usually uranium mines are secured facilities that you cannot enter - but you can enter these abandoned Soviet uranium mines in Poland. The tunnels you can tour aren't very radioactive - but they are filled with colorful blue rocks.

properties.name: Park Narodowy Gór Stołowych
properties.description: Stołowe Mountains National Park is the best National Park in Poland. The rocks on top of these mountains have eroded to form labyrinthian corridors, chasms, and towers. The Błędne Skały rock city literally looks like the tunnels of some alien civilization.

properties.name: Kopalnia Uranu Sztolnie Kowary
properties.description: Poland is a truly special place where you can tour Soviet uranium mines like this one. This mine has a yellow tinge to it, unlike the blue tinged uranium mine at Kletno.

properties.name: Zamek Książ
properties.description: This is the third largest castle in Poland is built on top of a mountain and surrounded by a garden complex, it's also Fürstenstein's castle - the basis of Frankenstein. The Nazis dug massive tunnels underneath the castle which are rumored to contain stolen treasures - and some are available for tour.

properties.name: Muzeum Motoryzacji Wena w Oławie
properties.description: This is the nicest car museum in Poland, probably because the 300+ vehicles here are stored indoors instead of rusting in a field.

properties.name: Park Krajobrazowy Orlich Gniazd
properties.description: The Polish King built this castle on top of the tall white rocks of the Rzędkowice Rocks formation. The castle now lays in ruins, the white masonry indistinguishable from the white cliffs and columns of the rocks.

properties.name: Muzeum Historii Polski Ludowej
properties.description: The Soviets ruled Poland through the collaborationist puppet government of the Polish People's Republic. The Museum of the history of the People's Republic of Poland contains statues that were torn down during decommunization, and the various Communist vehicles that roamed Poland from 1945-1989.

properties.name: Cohoes Falls
properties.description: Just North of Albany there is a waterfall that's 9 0ft tall and 1000ft wide -the only problem is that nearly 100% of the flow  is diverted for power generation- so it's only 'on' during the springtime.

properties.name: Palatul Parlamentului
properties.description: Communist dictator Nicolae Ceaușescu commissioned the largest and heaviest civilian administration building in the world - the Palace of the Parliament. The building is so large that much of it is still empty - despite being the center of the Romanian government. Some of the building is used as a museum complex, containing: the National Museum of Contemporary Art, and the Museum of the Palace of the Parliament.

properties.name: Muzeul Militar Național (Romania)
properties.description: Like most nations in the European thunderdome, Romania has seen a lot of war. Romania gets its name from the fact that the Romans conquered the lands known as Romania and turned it into a Roman province (Dacia). Romania's strategic location near Asian entrances to Europe means that it was overrun in its history by nomads on their way to pillage Europe ( Goths, Huns, Gepids, Avars, Slavs, Magyar, Pechenegs, Cumans, Uzes, Alans, Tatars), and by the Ottoman Empire. Romania united its divided principalities of Moldavia and Wallachia and achieved independence from the Ottoman empire in 1877. Romania then pillaged Bulgaria for some land in 1913, joined WW1 on the winning side to get land from Austria-Hungary in 1916, had land taken from them by the Soviet Union in 1940, joined the Nazis to get the land back in 1941,  were conquered by the communists in 1944, and overthrew their Communist dictatorship by force in 1989. If any of that sounds interesting to you, come see the armor and armored vehicles from Romania's long history of warfare at the National Military Museum.

properties.name: Palatul Primăverii
properties.description: Communism believes that each should give according to his ability, and receive according to his need - which is surely why Communist leader Nicolae Ceaușescu needed a luxurious mansion. As you gaze upon the opulent halls you may begin to understand the hatred that coursed through the oppressed and impoverished veins of the Romanian people when they overthrew Ceaușescu and executed him in 1989.

properties.name: Țiriac Collection
properties.description: Professional Tennis player Ion Țiriac leveraged his success in sports into a business empire - and he used the money to buy 170+ fancy cars for this museum.

properties.name: Salina Slănic
properties.description: Most mining museum tunnels are really short, but the galleries at the Slănic salt mine at 96m tall, and have been excavated since 1688.

properties.name: Castelul Peleș
properties.description: King Carol I of Romania was elected Prince of the the Romanian United Principalities in 1866, secured Romanian independence from the Ottoman Empire in 1877, and decided to build a luxury castle right next to the border of Austria-Hungary in 1883. When Romania annexed Transylvania from Austria-Hungary in 1918, it meant that the castle was located directly in the center of the country - exactly as Carol I had intended. Peleș Castle was spared destruction by the Communist regime, which means the lavish carved interiors remain are in good condition.

properties.name: Chipul lui Decebal
properties.description: A Romanian businessman carved a 180ft face of the last king of Dacia into a rock pillar in a valley in Romania.

properties.name: Castelul Corvinilor
properties.description: Corvin castle was built in 1440, but was rebuilt to look more like a fairytale gothic castle in 1868. Think of this as the gothic contemporary of Neuschwanstein Castle.

properties.name: Râpa Roșie
properties.description: The 410ft tall pink badlands of Râpa Roșie are only half a mile long, but they're incredibly out of place in the green hills of the Romanian countryside.

properties.name: Cheile Turzii
properties.street: Parcare Cheile Turzii Mihai Viteazu, Romania
properties.description: Turda Gorge is a narrow 300m tall canyon with near vertical walls - and the 2 mile hiking trail goes straight down the middle along the river.

properties.name: Salina Turda
properties.description: The Turda Saltworks have been active since 50BC, meaning the mining galleries are now hundreds of feet tall. So tall in fact that they put a ferris wheel at the bottom and built an underground lake where you can row boats in.

properties.name: Parcul Național Cheile Bicazului - Hășmaș
properties.description: The Bicaz Gorge is 5 miles long and 400 meters high, and the Romanians built highway DN12C straight through the middle of it. Bicaz gorge is part of Cheile Bicazului-Hășmaș National Park, which has hiking trails that stretch through the Bicaz gorges. You can see almost all of the gorge from your car, but there are some hiking trails through Cheile Bicajelului that you need to exit your vehicle to see.

properties.name: Parcul Natural Bucegi
properties.street: "Bucegi" Natural Park, Aleea Peștera Ialomiței, 137313 Moroeni, Romania
properties.description: Bucegi Natural Park encompasses the scenic Bucegi mountains, and features Ialomiței Cave - where a monastery has been built inside of a cave with a waterfall flowing out of it.

properties.name: Canionul Șapte Scări
properties.street: Strada Canionului, 505600 Timișu de Jos, Romania
properties.description: Usually narrow canyons with fast rivers running through them don't have hiking trails, but the Romanians built one anyway at Seven Ladders Canyon. Nearly the entire trail is built on metal pathways hammered into the canyon, or carved into the cliffside - giving a stunning view of the fast flowing waters that rage beneath you. As the name implies, there are ladders - some are right next to waterfalls.

properties.name: Liseberg
properties.description: Liserberg is a 1923 amusement park located on top of a hill in Gothenburg, Sweden. The rollercoasters Helix and Lisebergbanan dive down the hillside and wrap around the park, and the rest of the ride lineup makes this the largest amusement park in Sweden.

properties.name: Gyeongbokgung
properties.street: 161 Sajik-ro, Jongno District, Seoul, South Korea
properties.description: Gyeongbokgung Palace was built in 1395 to be the center of power for the Korean monarchy, but was neglected after it burned down in 1592. The palace was rebuilt to its former splendor in 1873, and is now a tourist attraction. The palace complex also hosts the Palace Museum of Korea and the National Folk Museum of Korea. Many artifacts of the Korean monarchy are found in the National Palace Museum of Korea located within the palace complex.

properties.name: Changdeokgung
properties.street: 185 Changgyeonggung-ro, Jongno District, Seoul, South Korea
properties.description: This is THE Korean palace. Changdeokgung was established in 1405 as the second royal palace, but became the main Korean palace after all of the palaces were destroyed in warfare. Changdeokgung Palace includes the Changgeyongung Palace as part of the "East Palace" complex in Seoul.

properties.name: War Memorial of Korea
properties.street: 29 Itaewon-ro, Yongsan District, Seoul, South Korea
properties.description: This is THE Korean military museum. South Korea's existence has been defined by its ongoing war with North Korea (which still isn't officially over, it's on hold). Ongoing mandatory military service for men means that the military is present in the minds of every South Korean, and this museum proudly shows off military aircraft, armored vehicles, and some smaller warships - including a replica turtle ship, North Korean infiltration craft, and Chamsuri-class patrol boat.  .

properties.name: Lotte World
properties.street: 240 Olympic-ro, Songpa District, Seoul, South Korea
properties.description: Have you ever wondered what Disneyworld would look like if it were run by a cyberpunk faceless megacorporation? Look no further. South Korean Chaebol Lotte Corporation opened their own Disneyland like amusement park. Lotte World shamelessly copies the architecture of Disney and Seaworld at Magic Island. The rest of the amusement park is located inside a stadium sized luxury shopping mall where Lotte products are for sale. Nearby, Lotte World Tower -the tallest building in South Korea (1,821ft) looms inescapably over the entire compound.

properties.name: Seoul Battleship Park
properties.street: South Korea, Seoul, Mapo-gu, Maponaru-gil, 407 서울함공원
properties.description: Battleship park is home to the Cold War era Ulsan-class frigate ROKS Seoul, the Cold War era  Dolgorae-class midget submarine SSM-053, and the Chamsuri-class patrol boat PKM-285. This is the largest collection of Naval warships in South Korea, and its right in the middle of Seoul.

properties.name: USS LST-1010
properties.street: 110-36 Daemyeonghang 1-ro, Daegot-myeon, Gimpo-si, Gyeonggi-do, South Korea
properties.description: Gimpo Ham Commercial Park is home to the LST 671 Un Bong (formerly USS LST-1010). This landing ship tank fought in WW2 at Okinawa, and the Vietnam War. The ship today is just a military museum, with the surrounding park full of military vehicles used aboard the ship.

properties.name: Bukhansan National Park
properties.street: 262 Bogungmun-ro, Seongbuk District, Seoul, South Korea
properties.description: There's hiking through temple and fortress covered mountains right next to downtown Seoul at Bukhansan National Park.

properties.name: Korea Railroad Museum
properties.description: Korea Railroad Corporation (Korail) is the government-owned railroad operator of Korea. Korail operates just about every train in Korea, including the metros, interurbans, and freight lines. The Korea Railroad Museum follows the history of Korean railway transport - which is mostly just a bunch of Japanese locomotives until 1945. The museum also has the carriages of the President of Korea and the Commander of the United Nations Forces In Korea.

properties.name: Hwaseong Fortress
properties.street: 825 Jeongjo-ro, Paldal-gu, Suwon-si, Gyeonggi-do, South Korea
properties.description: Hwaseong Fortress contains a pretty good looking Haengung Palace, but what makes this fortress interesting is that the walls surround nearly the entire town of Suwon - forming one continuous park.

properties.name: Everland
properties.street: 199 Everland-ro, Pogok-eup, Cheoin-gu, Yongin-si, Gyeonggi-do, South Korea
properties.description: Everland is the largest amusement park in South Korea - and yes it's operated by the Chaebol Samsung. Notably, this amusement park is themed after what Koreans think America, Europe, and the Middle East look like - which is charmingly stereotypical. Most of the rides are unremarkable, but T Express is regarded as one of the best wooden rollercoasters ever built.

properties.name: Samsung Transportation Museum
properties.street: 171 Everland-ro 376beon-gil, Cheoin-gu, Yongin-si, Gyeonggi-do, South Korea
properties.description: Korean Chaebol Samsung used to make cars, and horded them at the Samsung Transportation Museum. There's only 50 cars here, but the rest of the museum is dedicated to Fire and Marine Insurance.

properties.name: ROKS Cheonan Memorial
properties.description: The ROKS Cheonan was a Pohang-class corvette that was unexpectedly sunk by a North Korean submarine in 2010. The two halves of the ship were raised, and are now part of the West Sea Protection Hall at Pyeongtaek Naval Base. Similarly, the Chamsuri 457 was sunk by the North Koreans in 2002, but was raised and is on display here as well.  You need to book visits in advance - you are visiting an active naval base.

properties.name: USS Rogers (DD-876)
properties.street: 197-3 Unjeong-ri, Sinpyeong-myeon, Dangjin-si, Chungcheongnam-do, South Korea
properties.description: The WW2-era Gearing-class destroyer USS Rogers and the WW2-era LST-542-class tank landing ship USS Pender County both served in the Korean war in the United States Navy, but were later transferred to the Korean Navy. Both ships are docked as museum ships in Dangjin and can be toured.

properties.name: Daedunsan Provincial Park
properties.street: Sanbuk-ri, Unju-myeon, Wanju-gun, Jeonbuk State, South Korea
properties.description: You can hike up to the spines and columns of Daedunsan Provincial Park, or you can take the cable car. Near the top of the mountain is a bright red suspension bridge with a stunning view of the valley below and the mountain above.

properties.name: USS LST-849
properties.street: 32 Naehang 2-gil, Gunsan-si, Jeonbuk State, South Korea
properties.description: The LST-542 Landing Ship Tank USS LST-849 participated in the assault on Okinawa in WW2, and was later transferred to the Korean navy. Now it sits surrounded by military equipment and a patrol craft at the Jinpo Marine Theme Park in Gunsan. Despite being an American made ship, there are more LSTs available for tour in South Korea than there are in the United States.

properties.name: World Automobile & Piano Museum
properties.street: 1610 Jungsanganseo-ro, Andeok-myeon, Seogwipo-si, Jeju-do, South Korea
properties.description: You read that correct, it's a piano museum AND an automobile museum. It's 100+ cars and a bunch of fancy pianos - including a piano covered in 24 karat gold. You can also feed deer here.

properties.name: Wolchulsan National Park
properties.street: 280-43 Cheonhwangsa-ro, Yeongam-eup, Yeongam-gun, Jeollanam-do, South Korea
properties.description: Wolchulsan National Park looks like those stereotypical wispy paintings of mountains, and it includes a bright red suspension bridge on top of it. There's a lot of hiking trails here so you can see the interesting rock formations - including a trail that follows the crest of the mountain from beginning to end.

properties.name: Gangguan Port Turtle Ships
properties.description: This is THE Turtle ship museum. The medieval Korean Joseon Navy had a unique design called "Turtle Ships" - equipped with cannons and a spiked roof. Ganguan Port has 4 Joseon dynasty warships replicas, including 3 turtle ships and a Pan Ok-seon.

properties.name: KAI Aerospace Museum
properties.street: 78 Gongdan 1-ro, Sanam-myeon, Sacheon-si, Gyeongsangnam-do, South Korea
properties.description: Korean Aerospace Industries (KAI) is South Korea's only major aerospace manufacturer - formed from the merger all of other Korean aerospace companies. The KAI Aerospace Museum is the best collection of Korean War aircraft and armored vehicles in Korea, showing off 24 of the aircraft the United Nations Forces in Korea used to protect South Korea from North Korean invasion.

properties.name: National Maritime Museum of Korea
properties.description: The National Maritime Museum of Korea features the Dolgorae-class midget submarine (the first Korean submarine design for South Korea), the submersible Haeyang 250,  a replica of a Korean turtle ship, and a small aquarium. It's not the most exciting maritime museum as other museums in South Korea have full sized surface warships, but it's still interesting.

properties.name: ROKS Pohang (PCC-756)
properties.street: 389-18 송도동 Nam-gu, Pohang-si, Gyeongsangbuk-do, South Korea
properties.description: Unlike the ROKS Cheonan, this Pohang-class corvette is still afloat. The Cold War era Pohang-class corvette ROKS Pohang is the most modern intact warship available for tour in South Korea.

properties.name: Juwangsan National Park
properties.description: Juwangsan National Park is a hiking trail through a scenic rocky canyon filled with rushing river and waterfalls.

properties.name: Woraksan National Park
properties.description: The centerpiece of Woraksan National Park is Woraksan Mountain (3,589ft). The hiking trails head to the top of the mountain, which offers stunning views of the surrounding lakes and mountaintops. There's staircases all the way to the top of the mountain, but that doesn't mean it's an easy hike.

properties.name: Seoraksan National Park
properties.street: South Korea, Gangwon-do, Sokcho-si, Seoraksan-ro, 833 KR
properties.description: The mist covered peaks of Seoraksan National park soar over the surrounding pine forest covered valleys. The rocks here fare in interesting formations, such as those found at Ulsanbawi Rock, and Dinosaur Ridge. Well established hiking trails take you to most of what you want to see in the park

properties.name: Grykat e Osumit
properties.description: The Osumi Gorge is a 16-mile long near vertical gorge that has been carved by the Osum river. There's hiking, rafting, and various lookout points on the roadside so you can get up close and personal with the topography.

properties.name: Muzeu i Forcave të Armatosura
properties.description: After achieving independence from the Ottoman Empire in 1913, Albania collapsed into civil war as Greek nationalists sought independence in Epirus, and Muslim clerics who sought to reestablish Ottoman rule. The civil war led to Albania being invaded by Montenegro in 1914, Serbia in 1915, Austria-Hungary and Bulgaria (pursuing the Serbians) in 1915, and Italy and France (expelling the Austria-Hungarians and Bulgarians) in 1917. In WW2 Italy invaded Albania, and communist partisans liberated and took control of the country in 1944. Communist dictator Enver Hoxha aligned Albania with the Soviet Union, but then violently seized Soviet the Soviet submarine base at Vlorë following deteriorating relations. Albania returned to democracy in 1992, but the elected government created a nationwide Ponzi scheme which led to the Albanian Civil War in 1997. The Armed Forces Museum contains the equipment that was used to fight in the near continuous century of warfare in Albania.

properties.name: Bunk'Art 2
properties.description: Communist dictator Ener Hoxha built 14.7 bunkers per square mile in Albania to defend the country from invasion by NATO and the Warsaw Pact simultaneously. This command bunker has been turned into an art installation detailing the history of the Albanian secret police (Sigurimi) - and how they intended to keep their iron grip on the country even if the entire world was invading their doorstep.

properties.name: Bunk'Art 1
properties.description: This is THE Albanian bunker. Communist dictator Enver Hoxha built this nuclear fallout shelter into mount Dajti as part of the 173,000+ bunkers built in Albania during the Cold War. This bunker was intended for continuity of government in the event of invasion or nuclear war, and is so expansive that most of it has been converted into an art gallery.

properties.name: Lugina e Valbonës
properties.description: Valbona Valley National Park encompasses the Valbona river valley and its waterfalls and springs. The road down the valley lets you see most of the views, but if you want to see the best rock formations and the mountaintops, you'll have to hike.

properties.name: Naval Heritage Collection
properties.description: Porto Montenegro luxury yacht marina is home to the The Naval Heritage Collection Museum featuring some of the last surviving ships of the Yugoslav Navy: the Heroj-class attach submarine P-821, and the Una-class midget submarine Una.

properties.name: Kravica (vodopad)
properties.description: The 80ft Kravica Waterfall forms a bowl-like cascade through moss-covered rocks and trees into a lush swimming area. There's viewing platforms at the top and bottom of the falls so you can get a good look.

properties.name: Armijska Ratna Komanda D-0
properties.description: Even if nuclear war devastated the world, communist dictator Josip Broz Tito planned to keep the Slavic brotherhood of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia alive in the Ark atomic command bunker. The bunker escaped the destruction of the Bosnian war and is now one of the finest preserved examples of Yugoslavian communism.

properties.name: Tunel spasa
properties.description: After the fall of communism, the constituent ethnic republics of Yugoslavia decided they would be independent - the Serbians in the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina disagreed. Because the ethnic composition of Bosnia and Herzegovina was 32.5% Serbs, the fighting devolved into clashes  and genocide along ethnic lines. The capitol of Bosnia and Herzegovina remined under siege for nearly 4 years, and the Sarajevo Tunnel was dug by the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina to supply the besieged city with armaments, electricity, and oil - and to let civilians escape the warzone. The tunnel is now a museum with guided tours of the tunnel.

properties.name: Historijski muzej Bosne i Hercegovine
properties.street: 71000, Zmaja od Bosne 5, Sarajevo 71000, Bosnia & Herzegovina
properties.description: The Historical Museum of Bosnia and Herzegovina follows Bosnian history from liberation by communist partisans to the Siege of Sarajevo in the Bosnian War. The building itself is a dilapidated example of communist architecture, and there's also an armored train in the yard out back.

properties.name: Nacionalni park Una
properties.description: The waterfalls of Una National Park straddle the border of Bosnia and Herzegovina and Croatia. Roads and hiking trails follow the river as the cascades pour over rocks into pools - which you can go whitewater rafting in. For Americans keeping score at home, this most closely resembles a Pennsylvania river valley.

properties.name: Tehnički muzej Nikola Tesla
properties.description: Nikola Tesla Technical Museum is Croatia's main technical museum. The museum has a nice collection of machinery from the Federal Republic of Yugoslvaia, but also has the Italian WW2-era CB-class midget submarine Mališan.

properties.name: Nacionalni park Krka
properties.street: Šetnica Roški Slap - Visovac, 22324, Bogatić, Croatia
properties.description: The waterfalls at Krka National Park flow have lush trees growing in the middle of them, leading to tiered cascades next to verdant grey cliffs. The falls, cliffs, and caves at Roski is the main attraction, but there's also waterfalls in the town of Krka.

properties.name: Nacionalni park Plitvička jezera
properties.description: Colorful lakes are fed by waterfalls pouring off cliffs through greenery, leading to a tiered garden-like canyon crisscrossed with pedestrian footbridges.

properties.name: Amfiteatar u Puli
properties.description: It's like the Colosseum, but in Croatia. The Roman Empire tended to build large amphitheaters all across its provinces, this one is one of the best preserved ones remaining. Now it's a concert venue

properties.name: Baredine (jama)
properties.description: While not as impressive as the other Karst caves nearby in Slovenia, Baredine cave has all the stalactites and stalagmites you'd come to expect of caves.

properties.name: Galeb (brod)
properties.description: This is Josip Broz Tito's personal yacht. The ship was originally built as a banana boat in Italy, converted into an auxiliary cruiser during WW2, then transferred to Yugoslavia for use as the communist dictator's personal yacht.

properties.name: Matterhorn
properties.description: The Matterhorn is the tallest mountain in the area, and is distinctly triangular. The best view is from the Swiss side in Zermatt, as the other side just looks like a typical mountain ridge.

properties.name: Belgrade Fortress
properties.description: When Belgrade was founded, it existed only within the walls of this fortress - which grew over time as control passed between: Scordiscis, Romans, Bulgarians, Ottomans, Austrians, and Serbians. Belgrade Fortress is home to Kalemegdan Park, the Military Museum, Museum of Balkan Natural History, Luna Park (a small amusement park), and the Belgrade Zoo.

properties.name: Yugoslav monitor Sava
properties.street: Spomenik Obalskom Radniku, савско пристаниште, Beograd, Serbia
properties.description: The Austro-Hungarian Temes-class river Monitor Bodrog fired the first shots of World War 1 - shelling Belgrade and signaling the Austro-Hungarian invasion of Serbia. The river monitor later was captured by the Serbians and renamed Sava, then transferred to Yugoslavian service where it fought in WW2.

properties.name: Museum of Yugoslavia
properties.description: See how Yugoslavia lived and died at this museum - and by Yugoslavia they mean communist dictator Josip Broz Tito. This museum is also Tito's tomb.

properties.name: Aeronautical Museum (Belgrade)
properties.street: Aerodrom Nikola Tesla Beograd, 266 51, Surčin 11180, Serbia
properties.description: The Aeronautical Museum in Belgrade is Serbia's main air museum. The central building is well organized, and a careful curation of Yugoslavian aircraft - including the only remaining Fiat G.50, and the wreckage of the F-117 stealth fighter shot down in 1999 during the Kosovo War. The fields surrounding however are littered with hundreds of planes rusting in a field.

properties.name: KZ Crveni Krst
properties.description: After the Nazis invaded Yugoslavia in WW2, they quickly went about setting up concentration camps like Red Cross Concentration Camp as they began their mass killings of those that resisted. The communist Yugoslav Partisans liberated the camp in 1944, but by that point 10,000+ had been murdered there. The site has been preserved in its entirety, and is now a memorial where you can tour.

properties.name: Resava Cave
properties.description: The insides of Resava cave were formed by a sinking river, leaving behind a twisted and warped reddened cavern

properties.name: Belogradchik Fortress
properties.description: Belogradchik fortress is built among the columns and stacks of the Belogradchik Rocks. The Fortress makes a great start of the hiking trail through forest of the curvy rocky landscape, and the lookout points within the fortress itself offer the best views.

properties.name: Prohodna
properties.description: Prohodna Cave is called "The Eyes of God" because of the two eye shaped openings to the cave where beams of light shine down into the 150ft tall corridors.

properties.name: National Museum of Military History, Bulgaria
properties.description: Bulgaria is very proud of their military heritage despite being on the losing side of The Second Balkan War, World War One, World War Two, and the Cold War. The National Museum of Military History has a  collection of 5 Eastern Bloc missiles, 26 artillery pieces, 10 aircraft, and 19 armored vehicles.

properties.name: Museum of Socialist Art
properties.street: g.k. Iztok, ul. "Lachezar Stanchev" 7, 1756 Sofia, Bulgaria
properties.description: What if all art was government funded, directed, and rejected ornate depictions of reality? Come see where Bulgaria put all their Soviet monuments and artwork following decommunization at the Museum of Socialist Art.

properties.name: Melnik Earth Pyramids
properties.description: The mountains of southern Bulgaria have been melted away into sand-tinted hoodoos - which unusually exist in a lush landscape instead of the deserts of the American Southwest.

properties.name: Devil's Throat Cave
properties.description: Trigad Gorge is filled with fast moving water that has carved the cliffs into a wavy and narrow canyon. The river races down a waterfall into Devil's Throat Cave, where the river disappears. You an hike through the gorge to the cave in guided tours - but this is one of the places where you should really stay on the path for your own safety.

properties.name: Aviation Museum (Plovdiv)
properties.description: Bulgaria never really had an aviation industry, so the 65+ aircraft at the Plovdiv Aeronautics Museum was bought from other countries. Notably this museum has the only aircraft every produced in Bulgaria - the Lazarov Laz-7, and an Arado Ar 196 WW2 floatplane.

properties.name: Valley of the Thracian Rulers
properties.description: It's like a Bulgarian version of Egypt's Valley of the Kings. Thracians were the people in Bulgaria before Rome conquered them, and they buried their honored dead in this valley. 15 tombs are accounted for so far.

properties.name: Central Balkan National Park
properties.description: Central Balkan National Park is home to the tallest mountains in the Central Balkan range - which straddles the middle of Bulgaria. The mountains here are littered with waterfalls, including the Raysko Praskalo. There's hiking trails pretty much everywhere here.

properties.name: Devetashka Cave
