properties.description: Devetashka Cave is a 100ft tall cave with massive arches spanning its length. The sheer width and height of the cave makes it look like you're walking on the ceiling looking down at a valley.

properties.name: Retro Museum (Varna)
properties.street: Mladost, ul. "Akademik Andrei Saharov" 2, 9009 Varna, Bulgaria
properties.description: The Retro Museum is a museum of life under Communism in Bulgaria - it also happens to be located in a shopping mall. The museum has a nice collection of Eastern Bloc consumer automobiles (so many Ladas) and consumer goods - all they're in good condition instead of rusting.

properties.name: Bridal Veil Falls (Telluride)
properties.street: Public Parking and Trailhead Telluride, CO 81435
properties.description: Telluride Colorado sits in a box canyon, and at the end of its rests the 365ft tall Bridal Veil Falls. There's a hiking trail that will take you to the base of the falls, and to the decommissioned power station at the top.

properties.name: Tonto Natural Bridge State Park
properties.description: Tonto Natural Bridge is a 150ft wide,183ft tall, and 400ft long natural bridge that has a waterfall drizzling over its entrance. You can hike through the tunnel and into the valley, there's also an animal habitat.

properties.name: West Kern Oil Museum
properties.description: During the development of the American oil industry, California was the #3 oil-producing state. The wells and derricks at the West Kern Oil museum memorialize the dirty industry that California prefers to pretend doesn't exist. If you've watched the movie There Will Be Blood, then this is a pretty accurate representation of what they were up to.

properties.name: Musée Mécanique
properties.description: The Mechanical Museum in San Francisco contains 300+ historical Penny Arcade machinery, as well as arcade games and pinball machines.

properties.name: Chittenango Falls State Park
properties.description: Chittenango Falls State Park is dominated by the tiered 167ft tall Chittenango Falls. The Gorge Trail starts you off at the top of the falls and takes you to a pedestrian bridge spanning the base of the falls. It isn't the biggest waterfall in the State of New York, but it is the closest to the New York State Thruway.

properties.name: Taughannock Falls State Park
properties.description: The 215ft fall Taughannock Falls carved a massive bowl shaped gorge that leads to Cayuga Lake, and the Gorge Trail and Rim Loop Trail let you see everything from inside the gorge and above it.

properties.name: Sylvan Beach Amusement Park
properties.description: Sylvan Beach Amusement Park has been operating since 1879, making it one of the oldest amusement parks in the United States. Somehow, this park has been caught in a time vortex, and hasn't changed at all since the 1950s. Notable rides include a pitch black dark ride,  an extremely fast Himalaya painted with lascivious pictures, and a rollercoaster next to an Osprey nest.

properties.name: The Great Escape and Splashwater Kingdom
properties.description: The Great Escape and Splashwater Kingdom is a family amusement park that was originally founded as Storytown USA - a place with life sized replicas of Mother Goose children's stories. The amusement park now features 6 rollercoasters, including the historical 1948 Crystal Beach Comet which was relocated from Crystal Beach Canada.

properties.name: Darien Lake
properties.description: Typically, large thrill parks kill off local amusement parks in their surrounding areas; however, Darien Lake has been so incompetently run that the nearby competition of Niagara Amusement Park and Seabreeze remain standing. The Ride of Steel hypercoaster is good though, and the park has been improving in recent years. Mind Eraser and Boomerang are some of the most physically painful rollercoasters I have ever ridden - avoid them.

properties.name: DelGrosso's Park
properties.street: 4352 E Pleasant Valley Blvd, Tipton, PA 16684
properties.description: The DelGrosso pasta sauce company has been operating its own amusement park since 1946. There's nothing particularly special about it, but it is a pleasant family park and has spaghetti and a waterpark.

properties.name: Rock City Park
properties.description: Rock City is a privately owned rock formation where faults in the cliff have formed caves, small canyons, and passageways.

properties.name: Mt. Olympus Water & Theme Park
properties.street: 1881 Wisconsin Dells Pkwy B, Wisconsin Dells, WI 53965
properties.description: In the middle of Wisconsin there is an amusement park themed to the Greek Pantheon of Gods - featuring 5 rollercoasters (including one that dives underneath the parking lot), 5 go-kart tracks, and a massive waterpark. It's cheap - not great, and if you approach it that way you'll enjoy your time.

properties.name: Dells of the Wisconsin River
properties.description: The 100ft tall scenic rock formations lining the Wisconsin River would almost be worth stopping, if they hadn't been turned into a commercialized tourist trap where you are not given time to appreciate the beauty of what you see.

properties.name: Ausable Chasm
properties.description: Rainbow falls pours into rapids of the 150ft deep Ausable Chasm, a 2-mile long box canyon lined with hiking trails and crisscrossed by rope bridges. The chasm is owned by the local power company, and various tour packages allow rafting down the river, rappelling, and rock climbing.

properties.name: Kaaterskill Falls
properties.description: Kaaterskill Falls is a two-tiered 260ft tall waterfall with cavernous amphitheater like bowls at each level. The waterfall is located in the Catskills Mountains North Mountain Wild Forest, and has a parking lot that leads to a short trail, with access behind the waterfall itself.  There's no fences to protect you from walking off the cliff edges - so don't be stupid.

properties.name: Adventureland (Iowa)
properties.description: Adventureland is the largest amusement park in Iowa, with 7 rollercoasters - including the terrifyingly slow Tornado, the twisty Outlaw, the dark ride that technically counts as a rollercoaster - The Underground, and the scary looping monstrosity that is The Monster. Every other ride is a clone that can be found elsewhere,

properties.name: Mall of America
properties.description: The Mall of America opened as the largest mall in the world, and remains the largest mall in the United States. Minnesota is really so cold that a massive indoor city to shop in makes sense. There's also an amusement park anchoring the center of the mall - with 5 rollercoasters and a log flume. The rides at the amusement park are geared towards children, so know that going in.

properties.name: Valleyfair
properties.description: Valleyfair is the largest amusement park in Minnesota, with 8 rollercoasters - including the 207ft tall Wild Thing. While most of the rollercoasters here are unique designs (Wild Thing, Renegade, Excalibur, High Roller, Corkscrew) , they are fairly average in their execution.

properties.name: Michigan's Adventure
properties.description: Michigan's Adventure is Michigan's largest amusement park - and it represents the spirit of mediocrity and lack of ambition that permeates my home state. Though Michigan's adventure boasts 7 rollercoasters, only 3 of them are unique, the towering Shivering Timbers, the recently refurbished airtime machine Wolverine Wildcat, and Zach's Zoomer children's coaster. There's also a log flume that is nice.

properties.name: Worlds of Fun
properties.street: 4545 Worlds of Fun Ave, Kansas City, MO 64161
properties.description: Worlds of Fun is the closest amusement park to most of Kansas, and features 7 fairly decent rollercoasters - including the 207ft tall Mamba hypercoaster. Most of the rides here are unique designs, such as Prowler, Patriot, Zambezi Zinger, and Timber Wolf - however none are so standout to merit this park as a worldwide destination.

properties.name: Kentucky Kingdom
properties.description: Kentucky Kingdom is the largest amusement park in Kentucky, and boasts two world class rollercoasters: Lightning Run, and Windchaser. Kentucky Kingdom is a geographic oddity among amusement parks: a highway passes through the middle of the park, air traffic from the nearby Louisville International Airport has prevented anything tall from being built, and the parking lot is shared with the Kentucky State Fairgrounds and Kentucky Exposition Center.

properties.name: Quassy Amusement Park
properties.description: Quassy is a tiny amusement park in every way: the area it occupies is small, and so are all of its rides. Yet despite its small stature, the park packs a punch - featuring: a waterpark (including watercoaster), and 3 rollercoasters - including the Wooden Warrior.

properties.name: Lake Compounce
properties.description: Lake Compounce is the oldest amusement park in the United States - operating continuously since 1846. Of the 5 rollercoasters at the park, the star attraction is Boulder Dash - a rollercoaster that climbs 115ft up a hillside then races along the terrain by the lake. There's also the 1927 Wildcat - one of the oldest rollercoasters in the world.

properties.name: Morey's Piers
properties.description: Usually pier amusement parks operate only one pier - Morey's Piers operates 3. The piers feature 7 rollercoasters and a log flume - including a wooden rollercoaster built directly on the beach, and the only smooth Vekoma SLC ever built. This park would be worth stopping if the admission ticket wasn't over $100 USD - the same price as a season pass to most other amusement parks.

properties.name: Playland's Castaway Cove
properties.description: This tiny boardwalk amusement park somehow managed to cram 4 rollercoasters and a log flume in a 500x500ft plot of land. 3 of the rollercoasters are entirely unique designs

properties.name: Jolly Roger Amusement Park
properties.description: Jolly Roger Amusement park is an average amusement park, featuring 4 rollercoasters. The most notable thing about this park is the Splash Mountain Waterpark, which features a looping waterslide (it's an incline loop, but it doesn't feel that way when you're in it).

properties.name: American Dream (shopping mall)
properties.street: 1 American Dream Wy, East Rutherford, NJ 07073
properties.description: Someone decided that it was a good idea to built a massive indoor shopping mall in New York City - which itself it basically a massive outdoor shopping mall. Predictably, the American Dream mall is hauntingly empty liminal space - most of the storefronts are boarded up. Despite this, the mall features a skating rink, waterpark, amusement park, and indoor ski hill. The amusement park here features 5 of the most intense rollercoasters ever built - and due to no ventilation and no visible horizon they will leave you feeling sick to your stomach.

properties.name: Carowinds
properties.description: Carowinds is built across the state borders of North Carolina and South Carolina, and boasts 14 rollercoasters - making it the largest amusement park in the region. However, only 4 of the rollercoasters are good (Fury 325, Copperhead Strike, Afterburn, Thunderstriker), and the rest are actively terrible. The weather is hot, the lines are bad, and the operations are pitifully slow.

properties.name: Kings Dominion
properties.description: Kings Dominion is a clone of Kings Island with an inferiority complex. While King's Dominion lineup boasts 14 rollercoasters, only five of them are unique: including the gigacoaster Pantherian, the acclaimed Twisted Timbers, the recently refurbished Grizzly, the relocated Dominator, and the wing coaster Rapterra.

properties.name: John Boyd Thacher State Park
properties.description: Thacher state park is located on top of the 1300ft Helderberg Escarpment, with views of the Hudson and Mohawk Valleys. Indian Ladder Trail follows the escarpment, and lets you walk the edge of the cliff while streams of water flow down above you.

properties.name: Family Kingdom Amusement Park
properties.description: Family Kingdom is a beachside amusement park in the tourist trap town of Myrtle Beach, South Carolina. The park features 4 rollercoasters and a log flume, as well as a strong collection of thrill rides.

properties.name: Alabama Adventure & Splash Adventure
properties.description: Alabama Adventure is a small family theme park, and is dwarfed by the massive 121ft Rampage wooden rollercoaster. The rollercoaster's size has proven a financial liability for the park - which is mostly kept fiscally afloat by the sizeable waterpark.

properties.name: Penn's Cave
properties.street: 222 Penns Cave Rd, Centre Hall, PA 16828
properties.description: Penn's Cave is nestled in the rural valleys of Pennsylvania, and features a 55ft high 1300ft long cave that you tour by boat. This cave stands out in that the tour boat passes from the cave entrance all the way through to a lake.

properties.name: Bushkill Falls
properties.description: Bushkill Falls is a 100ft tall waterfall located in a narrow gorge in Pennsylvania. Despite being next to the Delaware Water Gap National Recreation Area, Bushkill Falls is privately owned. The trails here are wooden boardwalks that crisscross the gorge, putting you right next to the rapids in the river.

properties.name: Canobie Lake Park
properties.description: Canobie Lake Park has been operating since 1902, which means the rides here are a historical collection - including the 1936 Yankee Cannonball Rollercoaster, 1930s bumper cars, and 1978 rotor. There's 4 rollercoasters here in total, along with a log flume, and water park.

properties.name: Six Flags New England
properties.description: Six Flags bought Riverside Park in 1999, and promptly turned it into a poorly run and overcrowded park. There's 12 rollercoasters here, including the historical 1941 Thunderbolt, the Wicked Cyclone, and Superman The Ride hypercoaster.

properties.name: Six Flags Great Adventure
properties.street: 1 Six Flags Blvd, Jackson Township, NJ 08527
properties.description: Six Flags Great Adventure used to be Six Flags flagship park on the East Coast, and in classic Six Flags fashion they cut maintenance on their memorable rides until they had to be scrapped. 13 rollercoasters are located here, including the renowned wooden rollercoaster El Toro, and the hypercoaster Nitro.

properties.name: Clementon Park
properties.description: Clementon Park has been operated since 1907, and though the classic rides were demolished under Premier Parks mismanagement, the park has seen a recent resurgence spearheaded by the success of its waterpark.

properties.name: Sesame Place Philadelphia
properties.description: Surely a Sesame Street themed amusement park would be located near a city known for its safety and friendliness - and what friendlier place is there than Philadelphia? The city of brotherly love. It's a kid's theme park and waterpark with rides to match, but Oscar's Wacky Taxi Rollercoaster is well regarded for its compact thrills.

properties.name: Dutch Wonderland
properties.description: Dutch Wonderland is a kid's theme park featuring 3 rollercoasters and a log flume. The selling point is It's less crowded and with high customer service.

properties.name: Adventure Park USA
properties.description: The owner of this mini golf and go karting location REALLY wanted a rollercoaster - now he has 2.

properties.name: C.J. Barrymore's
properties.description: The entrance to this local amusement park is through a bar, the landscaping is from Home Depot, and extremely heavily armed security guards patrol the grounds. The 2 rollercoasters, drop tower, and 3 go-kart tracks are the main attractions here.

properties.name: Six Flags Over Georgia
properties.description: Six Flags Over Georgia was the third Six Flags park, and it lives up to the Six Flags reputation of poor maintenance and poor ride capacity. There are 12 rollercoasters here, including Twisted Cyclone, the hypercoaster Goliath, and the historical looping coaster Mindbender.

properties.name: Mid-America by Enchanted Parks
properties.description: Six Flags built this amusement park, neglected it, and sold it to Enchanted Parks. The park boasts 10 rollercoasters - including 3 original wooden rollercoasters.

properties.name: Six Flags Great America
properties.description: Marriot built Great America as an all americana themed amusement park - Six Flags turned it into a strip mall for low-capacity rollercoasters. There are 17 rollercoasters here, but only the hypercoaster Raging Bull and the Whizzer felt like they had any soul left in them.

properties.name: Lost Island Theme Park
properties.description: Lost Island operates the greatest waterpark in Iowa, and decided to expand into a theme park with 4 rollercoasters and a log flume.

properties.name: Frontier City
properties.street: 11501 N I- 35 Service Rd, Oklahoma City, OK 73131
properties.description: Frontier City is a small family amusement park with 5 rollercoasters and a log flume - including one of the last remaining Arrow Dynamics launched shuttle loops.

properties.name: Six Flags Over Texas
properties.street: Six Flags Over Texas, Arlington, TX 76011
properties.description: Six Flags Over Texas was the first Six Flags Park, and leads the nation in poor maintenance, overcrowding, and low capacity rides. The park features 13 rollercoasters, including the first Rocky Mountain Construction hybrid - the New Texas Giant, the classic looping coaster Shock Wave, and the first mine train rollercoaster ever - Runaway Mine Train. The first log flume is also located here.

properties.name: SeaWorld San Antonio
properties.description: SeaWorld San Antonio is a combined aquarium-amusement park and features 7 rollercoasters, including Steel Eel. There's also a launched log flume.

properties.name: Circuit of the Americas
properties.street: 9201 Circuit of the Americas Blvd, Del Valle, TX 78617
properties.description: Circuit of the Americas is one of the largest race tracks in the United States - and they expanded into developing a racetrack themed amusement park with 6 rollercoasters and a log flume.

properties.name: Galveston Island Historic Pleasure Pier
properties.description: The rollercoasters and rides at Galveston Island Historic Pleasure Pier dangle you over the ocean - so make sure your shoes and pockets are secure.

properties.name: Walt Disney World
properties.description: If you love spending $300 to get into an amusement park, waiting in line for an hour or more for every ride, and massive crowds - then Disney World is the place for you. The impeccably themed 4 amusement parks of Walt Disney World boast some of the most sophisticated amusement rides ever built - and they have been often copied. The artificial mountain built for Expedition Everest is the tallest mountain in the state of Florida. There's only 10 rollercoasters here - go to your local amusement park instead of wasting thousands at Disney.

properties.name: Universal Orlando
properties.description: Universal Orlando is the second most expensive amusement park in Orlando - you can pay $200 a day to experience long lines at the 3 well-themed amusement parks here. The 13 rollercoasters at Universal contain some of the best ever built - including the VelociCoaster, Hagrid's Magical Creatures Motorbike Adventure, Guardians of the Galaxy Cosmic Rewind, and Stardust Racers. However, the amount it costs to go here could pay for multiple vacations elsewhere.

properties.name: SeaWorld Orlando
properties.description: SeaWorld Orlando never really recovered from the reputational damage done by the animal-abuse documentary Black Fish, and as a result it is the cheapest major amusement park in Orlando. The aquarium life and 8 rollercoasters here are well regarded, especially the hypercoaster Mako, and the flying coaster Manta.

properties.name: Fun Spot America Orlando
properties.description: Fun Spot America is the bargain bin amusement parks in Orlando, it's pay per ride - and they are open until midnight. The 2 parks are located right next to Walt Disney World and Universal Studios Orlando, and feature 7 competently executed family rollercoasters.

properties.name: Busch Gardens Tampa Bay
properties.description: Busch Gardens Tampa charges prices as if they were still one of the best amusements parks in the United States, and not as if they have tried to cut guest experience to the bare minimum. The park is themed to Africa, and features various zoo exhibits of African animals. The rollercoasters here are all good, including Iron Gwazi - regarded as one of the best rollercoasters ever built.

properties.name: La Ronde (amusement park)
properties.street: Ile St-helene, 22 Chem. Macdonald, Montreal, Quebec H3C 6A3, Canada
properties.description: La Ronde is built on the remnants of the Expo 67 World's Fair - and maintenance hasn't been done since then. There's 9 rollercoasters here, but only Goliath and Vampire are any good. Traffic bottlenecks make entering and exiting La Ronde a nightmare - so plan ahead to have stuff to do while you either wait in your car, or for the subway.

properties.name: Lakeside Amusement Park
properties.description: Lakeside Amusement Park has been operating since 1908, and is the only park in the world that still maintains its theming reminiscent of the 1893 Chicago World's Fair. The park features 5 rollercoasters, including the 1940 Cyclone, and the 1955 Wild Chipmunk (which has no seatbelts).

properties.name: Six Flags Magic Mountain
properties.description: Six Flags Magic Mountain houses 18 rollercoasters - making it one of the largest amusement parks in the world. Don't be fooled by the number of rollercoasters - most are low capacity meaning there are long lines. Featuring the dueling hybrid coaster Twisted Colossus, the world's first multidimensional rollercoaster X2, the best flying coaster Tatsu, the first modern looping coaster New Revolution, and the suspended swinging coaster Ninja

properties.name: Disneyland
properties.description: Before Disneyland opened in 1953, amusement parks were considered trashy permanent carnivals instead of desirable destinations. Disneyland paid for the research and development of most modern ride designs through partial ownership of ride manufacturer Arrow Dynamics. Featuring 8 rollercoasters across 2 parks, including the world's first steel rollercoaster Matterhorn Bobsleds, and the first modern indoor rollercoaster - Space Mountain. Tickets are outrageously expensive - nearing $200 a day, the lines are long, and the park is crowded. Go to Knott's Berry Farm instead.

properties.name: Adventure City
properties.description: Adventure City was created as an extension of Hobby City, and is the cheapest children's park option in Southern California. There's also a replica of the White House here for some reason.

properties.name: Pacific Park
properties.street: 380 Santa Monica Pier, Santa Monica, CA 90401
properties.description: Pacific Park operates on a small section of Santa Monica pier on the glimmering beaches of the Los Angeles Metro Area. It is a full sized family amusement park, with a family rollercoaster, drop tower, and Ferris wheel.

properties.name: Universal Studios Hollywood
properties.street: 100 Universal City Plaza, Universal City, CA 91608
properties.description: Universal Studios Hollywood is actually located at the Universal Studios movie lot, costs a fortune to go to, and the lines are long. There's only 3 rollercoasters here, and the ride lineup is lacking. However, it's home to the first drifting rollercoaster - Fast & Furious - Hollywood Drift.

properties.name: SeaWorld San Diego
properties.street: 500 Sea World Dr., San Diego, CA 92109
properties.description: SeaWorld San Diego is the first SeaWorld amusement park, and features 5 rollercoasters. The SeaWorld chain is still suffering from the reputational damage from the animal abuse documentary Black Fish, so the prices are relatively affordable.

properties.name: Lagoon (amusement park)
properties.description: Lagoon has been operating since 1886 and is the only amusement park within a 5 hour drive - and is priced accordingly. The park features 10 rollercoasters, including the 1921 Roller Coaster, and the 210ft tall Cannibal. There's also an historical old-west Mormon town in here.

properties.name: California's Great America
properties.street: 4701 Great America Pkwy, Santa Clara, CA 95054
properties.description: California's Great America is located in the heart of the expensive real estate of Silicon Valley, which is why Six Flags sold the land underneath the park. The park and its 9 rollercoasters is slated for closure sometime after 2033 - though the Santa Clara city council has vowed not to rezone the land as to render closure useless.

properties.name: Six Flags Discovery Kingdom
properties.description: Six Flags Discovery kingdom has had a rocky history. Notably, the park deliberately lied about the height of The Flash: Vertical Velocity rollercoaster in flagrant violation of local ordinances, leading to it being condemned until it was shortened. This park features the worst rollercoaster in the United States - Kong, with the only notably good ride here being the Rocky Mountain Construction hybrid rollercoaster Joker.

properties.name: Gilroy Gardens
properties.description: Gilroy Gardens is a municipally owned amusement park run by the city of Gilroy, California. The park is mostly just a garden complex, but does feature 2 rollercoasters - including the Quicksilver Express mine train rollercoaster.

properties.name: Scandia Fun Center
properties.description: Don't confuse Scandia Fun Center is a minigolf course that expanded to include amusement rides. Notably, they have a one-of-a-kind wild mouse rollercoaster called Crazy Dane Coaster.

properties.name: Oaks Amusement Park
properties.street: 7805 SE Oaks Park Way, Portland, OR 97202
properties.description: Somehow Oaks Amusement Park can afford to operate on waterfront property in the middle of Portland. The park is closer to a permanent fair than a dedicated amusement park, but it does feature a looping rollercoaster.

properties.name: Elitch Gardens Theme Park
properties.description: Elitch Gardens is uniquely located in the downtown of Colorado - the only amusement park in the downtown of any American city. There's 5 rollercoasters here, and they're all mediocre or bad.

properties.name: Trimper's Rides
properties.street: 700 S Atlantic Ave, Ocean City, MD 21842
properties.description: Trimper's rides looks like a fairground, but it actually has been operating since 1893. Featuring a Bill Tracey haunted house and 2 rollercoasters.

properties.name: Havana Glen Park
properties.street: 135 Havana Glen Rd, Montour Falls, NY 14865
properties.description: While Watkins Glen State Park is the star of the waterfalls near Seneca Lake, Havana Glen Park offers a less crowded gorge and waterfall trail only 4 miles down the road.

properties.name: Fillmore Glen State Park
properties.description: Fillmore Glen State Park offers a short waterfall-filled gorge hike. It's not as good as nearby Buttermilk Falls State Park, Robert H. Trehman State Park, or Taughannock Falls State Park which are only 20 miles away - which is why it is significantly less crowded.

properties.name: High Falls Gorge
properties.description: High Falls Gorge is an 80ft deep chasm, with multiple ribbon falls cascading through it. The gorge has been lined with precariously balanced walkways that take you right through the heart of the gorge. The gorge is privately owned.

properties.name: National Museum of Transportation
properties.street: 2933 Barrett Station Rd, St. Louis, MO 63122
properties.description: By transportation, the National Museum of Transportation means 'trains', featuring 162 pieces of rolling stock, including: an Aerotrain, the EP-2 Bi-Polar, Union Pacific Big Boy, and a Zephyr streamliner. There's also 57 cars, and some buses, trolleys, subway cars, planes, etc.

properties.name: Méga Parc
properties.street: 5401 Bd des Galeries, Québec, QC G2K 1N4, Canada
properties.description: The Capital Galleries is home to Quebec's only indoor amusement park - Méga Parc. Featuring 2 indoor rollercoasters surrounded by an indoor ice skating rink.

properties.name: Meramec Caverns
properties.description: Meramec Caverns have been explored by humans since Pre-Columbian times - and is fabled to have been a hideout for Wild West outlaw Jesse James. The cave walls are covered in popcorn like formations, and long stalactites reach down from the seven story high ceiling. Tours take over an hour, it's a big and well lit cave - unlike the caves nearby at Meramec State Park.

properties.name: Calaway Park
properties.street: 245033 Range Rd 33, Calgary, AB T3Z 2E9, Canada
properties.description: Calaway Park is the amusement park Calgary has. The park is partially Flintstones styled, and has 3 unoriginal rollercoasters and an original log flume

properties.name: West Edmonton Mall
properties.street: 8882 170 St NW, Edmonton, AB T5T 4J2, Canada
properties.description: Edmonton is really really cold, which is why they have a massive mall here with a waterpark, ice skating rink, and 4 rollercoasters at the Hasbro themed Galaxyland Amusement park

properties.name: Santa's Village (Bracebridge)
properties.street: 8882 170 St NW, Edmonton, AB T5T 4J2, Canada
properties.description: Long ago in the past, there were many Santa Claus themed children's amusement parks. Santa's Village in Bracebridge has stood the test of time since 1961, and even expanded with a brand new 66ft tall rollercoaster.

properties.name: Oil Museum of Canada
properties.street: 2423 Kelly Rd, Oil Springs, ON N0N 1P0, Canada
properties.description: In 1858 James Miler William's water well filled with oil, which he developed into the first commercial oil well in North America. The town is called Oil Springs because oil literally springs out of the ground when you walk on it. Come learn about the early oil industry - which was later got its modern start at Drake Well in Pennsylvania in 1859.

properties.name: Grand Falls Gorge
properties.street: 125 Manse Rd, Grand Falls, NB E3Z 2X4, Canada
properties.description: Canadians dammed the Grand Falls, so the remaining waterflow from the 75ft tall waterfall is pitiful - but the granite gorge remains striking. The Grand Falls Gorge Trail lets you follow the rim of the gorge, and take in some nice views.

properties.name: Sleeping Giant Provincial Park
properties.street: R R 1, Pass Lake, ON P0T 2M0, Canada
properties.description: The steep granite cliffs of Sleeping Giant Provincial Park look like the silhouette of a giant laying on its back when viewed from Thunder Bay, Ontario. The park itself has hiking trails that take you along the rocky coast and up on top of the giant.

properties.name: Thorpe Park
properties.street: Staines Rd, Chertsey KT16 8PN, United Kingdom
properties.description: Thorpe Park is built on and island in the middle of a flooded gravel pit, and sports 8 rollercoasters - including the tallest and fastest rollercoaster in the UK- Hyperia, and Colossus - a rollercoaster with 10 inversions. Most of the rides here are fairly intense, and not aimed at a general audience.

properties.name: Chessington World of Adventures
properties.description: Chessington World of Adventures is a combine zoo-amusement park - featuring 4 rollercoasters including Vampire - one of the first suspended swinging coasters.

properties.name: Drayton Manor Resort
properties.street: Drayton Manor Dr, Fazeley, Drayton Bassett, Tamworth B78 3TW, United Kingdom
properties.description: Drayton Manor is a family amusement park with 5 rollercoasters, including Gold Rush - a rollercoaster that changes track configurations between ride cycles.

properties.name: Flamingo Land Resort
properties.description: Flamingo Land is a combined amusement park and zoo, featuring 10 rollercoasters - and some of them are even good.

properties.name: Red Canyon (Dixie National Forest)
properties.description: Red Canyon is another forest covered red rock canyon sandwiched between Bryce Canyon National Park and its less popular sibling Cedar Breaks National Monument. Red Canyon features the same pinnacles, hoodoos, and columns that you'll find at the nearby National Parks, but its much less busy due to being much less developed - which means you can get permits for off-road-vehicles and mountain bikes. You can see a lot of the highlights along Scenic Byway 12

properties.name: Fantasy Canyon
properties.description: The rocks at Fantasy Canyon have eroded to look like angry driftwood. The road to get there is unpaved,  and the canyon is fragile. This is one of those "Middle of Nowhere" kind of places, so plan accordingly.

properties.name: Cumberland Falls State Resort Park
properties.description: Cumberland Falls State Resort Park is home to the 69ft Cumberland Falls and the 44ft Eagle Falls alongside an escarpment. There are short hiking trails which will take you alongside both of the falls.

properties.name: Pratt's Falls Park
properties.description: Pratt's Falls is a 137ft waterfall with a parking lot at the top, and a hiking trail to the bottom. It's a less impressive waterfall compared to nearby Chittenango Falls State Park.

properties.name: Eternal Flames Falls
properties.street: Eternal Flame Hiking Trail, Orchard Park, NY 14127
properties.description: The 30ft Eternal Flames Falls is unimpressive except for the fact that there's a candle-sized natural fire burning behind it. The natural gas plume sometimes gets extinguished, so bring a lighter.

properties.name: Canyon Sainte-Anne
properties.street: 206 route 138 est, Saint-Joachim, QC G0A 3X0, Canada
properties.description: Canyon Saint-Anne is a 243ft tall waterfall running through an even deeper gorge. Surprisingly, this park wasn't developed until 1973, but is now crisscrossed with pedestrian bridges and viewing platforms.

properties.name: Horseshoe Canyon (Alberta)
properties.street: Township Rd 284, Kneehill County, AB T0M 2A0, Canada
properties.description: The badlands of Horseshoe Canyon are more compact and exemplary of what you would expect the badlands surrounding Drumheller to look like - and more importantly you can hike down into the middle of them.

properties.name: Gila Cliff Dwellings National Monument
properties.description: Native Americans carved houses into the alcoves of the gorges of Gila National Forest - and now you can hike right up to them. Don't be deceived by the forested mountains and babbling brooks - you are in the middle of a desert - plan accordingly.

properties.name: Bond Falls
properties.street: Bond Falls Scenic Site, Trout Creek, MI 49967
properties.description: Bond Falls is a 50ft tall waterfall that aggressively spills over a wide swath of rock - engulfing islands of trees as it streams down the Middle Branch Ontonagon River. Boardwalks surround the base of the falls, while trails let your get close to the top.

properties.name: Copper Falls State Park
properties.description: The copper soaked granite gorges and waterfalls of Copper Falls State Park aren't very tall, but they are unique.

properties.name: Aguasabon Falls & Gorge
properties.street: 2 Aguasabon Gorge Rd, Terrace Bay, ON P0T 2W0, Canada
properties.description: The 100ft tall Aguasabon Falls pours into the narrow Agausabon Gorge. This waterfall is not really near anything, so it only has one viewing platform - but it's the only really interesting thing to do on this section of the Trans Canada Highway.

properties.name: Parc le Trou de la Fée
properties.street: 100 Rte du Trou-de-la-Fée, Saint-André-du-Lac-Saint-Jean, QC G0W 2K0, Canada
properties.description: Parc le Trou de la Fée (Fairy Hole Park) is a canyon full  of waterfalls and caves connected by a walkway that follows the river. You would think there would be more information on it - but there is not.

properties.name: Val-Jalbert
properties.street: 95 Rue Saint-George, Chambord, QC G0W 1G0, Canada
properties.description: It's a Canadian ghost town bisected by a 236ft tall waterfall (Ouiatchouan Falls). Val Jalbert is a historical ghost town built around the remains of an abandoned papermill in the deep forests of northern Quebe - the ruins of the buildings are now a historical village, but everything is still decaying and falling apart exactly as it was in 1929.

properties.name: Matthiessen State Park
properties.description: Matthiessen State Park is the less pretty and less popular sister of Starved Rock State Park. The canyons (Upper and Lower Dells) here are muddier, and the waterfalls less impressive. However, it is still beautiful.

properties.name: Olney City Park
properties.description: Olney, Illinois has been strategically protecting a colony of pure-white squirrels in its city park since 1902.

properties.name: Shades State Park
properties.description: Shades State Park is the less popular and less pretty sister of Turkey Run State Park. Though the park boasts 5 ravines with interesting rock formations, 100ft tall cliffs along the river, and trickling waterfalls.

properties.name: Devils Rope Barbed Wire Museum
properties.description: This is THE barbed wire museum. Modern barbed wire was invented in the United States as a livestock deterrent for areas that lacked traditional fencing materials, but soon found use in prisons and trench warfare. This is one of 2 barbed wire museum in the United States, with the other being the Kansas Barbed Wire Museum.

properties.name: Williamsport Falls
properties.street: Fall Street &, N Monroe St, Williamsport, IN 47993
properties.description: Williamsport Falls is a 90ft tall waterfall with an overhang nearly perfectly at its waist. It doesn't look that impressive in pictures, but when it is towering over you then you will realize how tall 90ft is.

properties.name: Clifty Falls State Park
properties.description: The 4 waterfalls of Clifty Falls aren't the most powerful waterfall in Indiana, however the hiking trails snake along the rim and inside of the 200ft deep Clifty Creek Canyon - including passing through a tunnel

properties.name: Emerald Park (Ireland)
properties.street: Emerald Park, Kilbrew, Ashbourne, Co. Meath, A84 EA02, Ireland
properties.description: This is the largest amusement park in Ireland, and also one of the newest amusement parks in Europe. Featuring 6 rollercoasters and a log flume.
